source_documents.title: Kinetics of Excimer Electrogenerated Chemiluminescence of Pyrene and 1-Pyrenebutyricacid 2-Ethylhexylester in Acetonitrile and an Ionic Liquid, Triethylpentylphosphonium Bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide

reference_evidence_units.quote: the broad PL emission with the maximum around 480 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ
reference_evidence_units.conditions: PLQ concentration series in MeCN and the ionic liquid [P2225][TFSI].
reference_evidence_units.statement: The approximately 480 nm broad emission increases with concentration; neat PLQ is dominated by excimer emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Pyrene is a comparator; its values are not PLQ measurements.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the formation of excimers is a diffusion-controlled process.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ and pyrene
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Concentration-dependent PL decay fits and diffusion coefficients from electrochemistry.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Fitted excimer formation rates and diffusion-limited estimates agree; the much more viscous ionic liquid suppresses excimer formation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Diffusion-controlled intermolecular encounters are distinct from restriction of internal rotation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: a 0.3−0.4 ns delay of the excimer emission in neat PLQ
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Neat PLQ compared with dilute PLQ monomer emission; main text describes SI Fig. S2.
reference_evidence_units.statement: A short delayed rise is reported for neat PLQ, interpreted as an orientational rearrangement before excimer formation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The raw SI decay is not available here; do not confuse this subnanosecond formation delay with delayed fluorescence from triplet states.

reference_evidence_units.quote: four different dimer structures with stacked pyrene rings are possible
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ dimers
reference_evidence_units.conditions: PBE0/TZVp potential energy curves with assumed parallel-stacked rings, Fig. 5 and Table 3.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Three modeled PLQ configurations have an excited-state energy minimum at 3.50 angstrom; a sterically disfavored configuration shifts to 4.95 angstrom.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The stacked starting geometry is assumed to reduce cost. These are computed geometries, not an experimental crystal structure.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the enhancement of kr
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ versus pyrene
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Monomer PL lifetime and integrating-sphere yield at 10 micromolar; Table 2.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source derives radiative and nonradiative rates and attributes the larger PLQ radiative rate to symmetry breaking by its substituent; ionic-liquid interactions also enhance the radiative rate.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Main prose gives a MeCN PLQ lifetime near 210 ns whereas Table 2 lists 198 ns. This discrepancy should be resolved before adopting a precise lifetime.

reference_evidence_units.quote: can be ascribed to the suppression of vibrational relaxations
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ and pyrene
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Comparison of inferred nonradiative rates in viscous ionic liquid and MeCN.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors attribute the reduced nonradiative rate in the ionic liquid to suppressed vibrational relaxation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This is an indirect interpretation of rate estimates, not resolved vibrational dynamics or a general aggregation-induced RIM mechanism.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the direct formation of the monomer S1 states through the electron transfer prevails
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ and pyrene ECL
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Electrogenerated radical-ion annihilation, Marcus-rate analysis and dimer energies.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The favored proposed ECL route first creates the monomer excited state by electron transfer, followed by diffusion-driven excimer formation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This is electrode-driven electron transfer, not evidence for a photoinduced intramolecular PET quencher. Continuum-solvent and electronic-coupling assumptions limit the kinetic model.

reference_evidence_units.quote: a depletion around 495 nm was observed.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ and pyrene ECL
reference_evidence_units.conditions: High-concentration ionic-liquid solutions under square-wave electrochemical excitation.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The spectral depletion is attributed to reabsorption by accumulated radical anions, not a separate emitting mechanism.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This artifact is concentration- and excitation-dependent; do not turn two apparent peaks into two excited-state mechanism labels.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Retain the authors' suppressed vibrational relaxation explanation under viscous-solvent conditions, with its indirect evidential status.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Electron transfer generates excited states in the ECL protocol. This broad ET-family assignment is conditional on electrochemical excitation, not conventional intramolecular photoinduced PET.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Excimer formation is the central explanation supported by concentration trends, kinetics and bounded dimer calculations.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Lifetime/yield-derived rates and symmetry/solvent effects support a rate-balance interpretation; reabsorption must not be misclassified as state redistribution.

mechanism_decisions.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Retain the authors' suppressed vibrational relaxation explanation under viscous-solvent conditions, with its indirect evidential status.

source_documents.title: Photophysical Properties of an Azine-Linked Pyrene− Cinnamaldehyde Hybrid: Evidence of Solvent-Dependent Charge-Transfer-Coupled Excimer Emission

reference_evidence_units.quote: the addition of water diminished the CT band, and the high-energy band experienced increment in intensity.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PYNC
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Methanol/water and acetonitrile/water mixtures with increasing water fraction.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Increasing water changes the two emission bands in opposite directions.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Solvent polarity and aggregation change together; the titration alone does not distinguish them.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the increasing concentration of probe in solvents other than water contributes to increment of the high-energy emission band
reference_evidence_units.subject: PYNC
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Concentration series in methanol, water and acetonitrile.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The high-energy emission grows with concentration outside water.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The statement concerns concentration dependence, not a directly measured excited dimer structure.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the high-energy band diminishes gradually with an increment of a band at ∼590 nm.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PYNC
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Increasing PEG400 fraction in water, used as a viscosity perturbation.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The two bands respond oppositely as PEG400 is added.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: PEG400 changes dielectric properties as well as viscosity.

reference_evidence_units.quote: increment of viscosity freezes the single-bond rotational motions in PYNC
reference_evidence_units.subject: PYNC
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Water/PEG400 mixtures.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors invoke restricted rotation to explain enhancement of the CT emission component.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This is a source interpretation of a mixed solvent perturbation, not a measured torsional trajectory.

reference_evidence_units.quote: PYNC was found to be totally nonfluorescent in the solid state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PYNC
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Solid-state emission compared with emission in water.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Solid PYNC is nonfluorescent under the reported comparison.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This limits a generic AIE assignment but does not rule out every aggregate-related excited state.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the high-energy band was due to the pyrene excimer and the polarity-sensitive band was due to excited-state intramolecular charge transfer in PYNC.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PYNC
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Reported solvent, concentration, viscosity and solid-state comparisons.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source assigns separate bands to excimer emission and intramolecular CT.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: These are the paper's assignments, not an independent confirmation by this pipeline.

reference_evidence_units.quote: a biexponential nature of decay was observed in all solvents except water, where monoexponential decay having a considerably long lifetime was obtained
reference_evidence_units.subject: PYNC
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 375 nm excitation, detection at the assigned excimer band.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The decay at the assigned excimer band depends on solvent.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The source discusses solvent complexes; lifetime components should not be treated as uniquely identified species.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Upon deconvoluting the decay profiles, lifetime components were obtained that fall below the instrumental response function.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PYNC
reference_evidence_units.conditions: CT-band fluorescence decay following 375 nm excitation.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source reports fitted CT lifetime components below the instrumental response function.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Do not present these components as independently resolved CT formation or transfer times. The source instead discusses average lifetimes.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Motion restriction is an enabling explanation of viscosity-enhanced CT emission, not a general claim that PYNC is AIE-active.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The separate polarity-sensitive CT emission is the other central source interpretation.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The excimer interpretation is central to the paper and supported by several target-specific perturbations.

source_documents.title: Aggregation-induced emission (AIE) behavior and thermochromic luminescence properties of a new gold(I) complex

reference_evidence_units.quote: an emission band was observed with lmax at 402 nm and 425 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: gold(I) complex 1
reference_evidence_units.conditions: EtOH/water at approximately 20 micromolar, excitation 310 nm.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Water addition first enhances blue emission; higher water fractions decrease blue emission and produce a 559 nm band.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The response is nonmonotonic, with further water eventually weakening the yellow-green emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: We speculate that two kinds of nano-aggregates might be formed
reference_evidence_units.subject: gold(I) complex 1
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Water-fraction-dependent spectra and main-text description of DLS in SI.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors propose different aggregates and packing-dependent Au-Au interactions as the cause of color changes.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The authors' speculative wording is retained; DLS does not resolve Au-Au distances in the emitting aggregates.

reference_evidence_units.quote: a broad emission band, with a maximum wavelength of 530 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: gold(I) complex 1 solid
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Heating above approximately 55 degrees C, then cooling to 25 degrees C, Fig. 2.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The blue solid develops a broad 530 nm band on heating and recovers the original emission after cooling.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Thermochromism is observed; a particular amorphous packing geometry is not directly established by this observation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: ligand-to-metal–metal charge transfer (LMMCT) excited state
reference_evidence_units.subject: gold(I) complex 1 solid
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Interpretation of thermally induced lower-energy emission.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Aurophilic interactions and an LMMCT state are proposed for the yellow-green emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This metal-associated assignment does not itself establish a measured triplet lifetime or phosphorescence.

reference_evidence_units.quote: no obvious intermolecular gold–gold interaction is indicated.
reference_evidence_units.subject: gold(I) complex 1 initial crystal
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Reported X-ray packing, Fig. 3; initial crystal before thermal transformation.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The initial crystal has Au-Au separations reported as 3.782 and 4.83 angstrom, too long for the strong aurophilic contacts proposed for the emitting transformed material.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Do not claim the initial crystal directly proves the short Au-Au contact of the heated or aggregated phase; graph identity is not adjudicated here.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Cooling then made the amorphous phase rearrange into the more stable crystalline phase.
reference_evidence_units.subject: gold(I) complex 1
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Reversible thermal emission cycle.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The paper interprets recovery as a packing/phase rearrangement after cooling.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: A bounded phase explanation; obtain SI or additional phase characterization before treating all phase assignments as independently verified.

reference_mechanisms.label: PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Changes in assembly and solid-state packing are central to the source explanation; specific transformed geometries are inferred.

reference_mechanisms.rationale: The broad family covers the proposed aurophilic metal-associated LMMCT state. Do not equate this with independently measured triplet dynamics.

source_documents.title: Insight into the strong aggregation-induced emission of low-conjugated racemic C6-unsubstituted tetrahydropyrimidines through crystal-structure-property relationship of polymorphs

reference_evidence_units.quote: THPs 1–3 in different organic solvents (cyclohexane, ethanol and acetonitrile etc.) are practically non-emissive
reference_evidence_units.subject: THPs 1-3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Solutions in the named solvents compared with crystalline polymorphs.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The series is nearly nonemissive in solution but emissive in crystals.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Qualitative solution comparison; do not infer measured solution rate constants from negligible emission.

reference_evidence_units.subject: THP 1
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 1b and 1c; Table 1, integrating-sphere yields at 380 nm and lifetimes at 360 nm.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Emission peaks 434/484 nm, yields 72/93%, lifetimes 7.1/14 ns; derived kr 1.01/0.66 and knr 0.39/0.05 in units of 10^8 s^-1.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Full table columns were read with their headers, not as an unassigned numerical sequence. Rates are derived from yield/lifetime, not direct transition measurements.

reference_evidence_units.quote: all polymorphs with longer lem values, 1c, 2c0, 3b and 3c, show an unpaired packing mode
reference_evidence_units.subject: THPs 1-3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Single-crystal structures, paired RS versus unpaired RR/SS packing.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Packing arrangements differ between polymorphs without changing molecular connectivity.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: A correlation with emission is not unique proof of one excited-state process. The extracted prime is represented as 0.

reference_evidence_units.quote: restriction of intramolecular motion (RIM) by intra- and inter- molecular interactions
reference_evidence_units.subject: THPs 1-3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Source explanation of the solution-to-aggregate change.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors assign reduced nonradiative loss to motion restriction.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Retain as an interpretation supported by crystal/rate comparisons, not a directly measured molecular trajectory.

reference_evidence_units.quote: both a local excitation state (LE) and an intramolecular charge transfer excitation state (ICT) exist
reference_evidence_units.subject: THP 1 polymorphs; analogous orbitals reported for THPs 2 and 3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: HOMO/LUMO calculations based on crystal conformations; main Figure 6 is 1b/1c, other polymorphs cited in Figure S5.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors interpret the orbital distributions as LE/ICT contributions.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: For THPs 2 and 3, the analogous orbital figures are reported in missing SI; they are not independently inspected here.

reference_evidence_units.quote: improved electronic coupling via through-bond and through-space pathways
reference_evidence_units.subject: THPs 1-3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Computed orbitals combined with Table 1 rates.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors associate increased radiative rates with electronic coupling and favorable LE/ICT processes.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No measured solution kr is available in the selected evidence; the enhancement relative to solution is interpreted.

reference_evidence_units.quote: they can form emissive poly- morphs by through-bond and through-space electron coupling in aggregates
reference_evidence_units.subject: THPs 1-3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Source conclusion integrating polymorph structures, spectra and calculations.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Intermolecular packing and electronic coupling are central to the authors' aggregate-emission account.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Generic coupling is not by itself a resolved H/J exciton, excimer or exciplex; preserve that taxonomy boundary.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Motion restriction is the source's central nonradiative explanation.

reference_mechanisms.label: PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The paper explicitly compares packing arrangements and their optical consequences for identical molecular connectivity.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: LE/ICT mixing contributes to the electronic account, with target-specific and series-level calculations distinguished.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The source quantitatively separates radiative and nonradiative rates; this overlaps the RIM/packing explanation rather than being an independent cause.

reference_evidence_units.subject: THPs 1-3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Solutions in the named solvents compared with crystalline polymorphs.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The series is nearly nonemissive in solution but emissive in crystals.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Qualitative solution comparison; do not infer measured solution rate constants from negligible emission.

reference_evidence_units.subject: THP 3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 3p, 3b and 3c; Table 1, integrating-sphere yields at 380 nm and lifetimes at 360 nm.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Emission peaks 425/445/468 nm, yields 30/20/52%, lifetimes 2.9/2.3/7.6 ns; derived kr 1.03/0.87/0.68 and knr 2.41/3.48/0.63 in units of 10^8 s^-1.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Full table columns were read with their headers, not as an unassigned numerical sequence. Rates are derived from yield/lifetime, not direct transition measurements.

reference_evidence_units.quote: all polymorphs with longer lem values, 1c, 2c0, 3b and 3c, show an unpaired packing mode
reference_evidence_units.subject: THPs 1-3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Single-crystal structures, paired RS versus unpaired RR/SS packing.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Packing arrangements differ between polymorphs without changing molecular connectivity.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: A correlation with emission is not unique proof of one excited-state process. The extracted prime is represented as 0.

reference_evidence_units.quote: restriction of intramolecular motion (RIM) by intra- and inter- molecular interactions
reference_evidence_units.subject: THPs 1-3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Source explanation of the solution-to-aggregate change.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors assign reduced nonradiative loss to motion restriction.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Retain as an interpretation supported by crystal/rate comparisons, not a directly measured molecular trajectory.

reference_evidence_units.quote: both a local excitation state (LE) and an intramolecular charge transfer excitation state (ICT) exist
reference_evidence_units.subject: THP 1 polymorphs; analogous orbitals reported for THPs 2 and 3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: HOMO/LUMO calculations based on crystal conformations; main Figure 6 is 1b/1c, other polymorphs cited in Figure S5.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors interpret the orbital distributions as LE/ICT contributions.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: For THPs 2 and 3, the analogous orbital figures are reported in missing SI; they are not independently inspected here.

reference_evidence_units.quote: improved electronic coupling via through-bond and through-space pathways
reference_evidence_units.subject: THPs 1-3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Computed orbitals combined with Table 1 rates.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors associate increased radiative rates with electronic coupling and favorable LE/ICT processes.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No measured solution kr is available in the selected evidence; the enhancement relative to solution is interpreted.

reference_evidence_units.quote: they can form emissive poly- morphs by through-bond and through-space electron coupling in aggregates
reference_evidence_units.subject: THPs 1-3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Source conclusion integrating polymorph structures, spectra and calculations.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Intermolecular packing and electronic coupling are central to the authors' aggregate-emission account.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Generic coupling is not by itself a resolved H/J exciton, excimer or exciplex; preserve that taxonomy boundary.

reference_evidence_units.quote: formed the organic analogues, dendrimers D3a,b and D5
reference_evidence_units.subject: D5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Demetallation of precursor D4; Scheme 4 and synthesis description.
reference_evidence_units.statement: D5 is the demetallated organic analogue, not one of the organoiron dendrimers used in electrochemical comparisons.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This establishes the source designation, not verification of the inherited SMILES.

reference_evidence_units.quote: there is no interaction between the two pyrenyl units in the ground state to form dimers.
reference_evidence_units.subject: D3a,b, D5, D9 and D13 in solution
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Monomer-like absorption across organic solvents.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors use largely unchanged absorption shape to argue against ground-state dimers in these solution conditions.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This does not exclude ground-state aggregation in high-water mixtures; an absorption-based assignment is not direct intermolecular-distance measurement.

reference_evidence_units.quote: When dendrimer D5 was excited at 343 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: D5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 10 micromolar, THF/water series, Figs. 18-19.
reference_evidence_units.statement: D5 shows pyrene monomer bands at 377 and 398 nm and an approximately 470 nm band enhanced by aggregation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Separate this target-specific result from the more extensively analyzed D3a and D3b.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The values were 0.54 in pure THF and 2.66 in the 1 : 9 THF/water mixture.
reference_evidence_units.subject: D5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Excimer/monomer intensity ratio in Figs. 18-19; excitation 343 nm.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The reported excimer/monomer ratio increases from 0.54 to 2.66 with water-induced aggregation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: A ratio of emission intensities is not an absolute fluorescence quantum yield.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the pyrene is attached directly to the zero generation without flexible chain.
reference_evidence_units.subject: D5 versus D3a/D3b
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Comparison of dendrimer linkage design and spectra.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors distinguish D5 from the flexible-chain derivatives and relate its behavior to pyrene proximity and excimer formation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Do not copy the flexible-chain RIM explanation or its thresholds from D3a/D3b directly to D5.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This suggests that the excimer emission is due to intramolecular interactions
reference_evidence_units.subject: D5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: High-water aggregation; Fig. 19.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source suggests intramolecular pyrene interactions contribute to excimer emission under aggregation conditions.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The intramolecular assignment is tentative; no target-specific time-resolved separation from intermolecular excimers is demonstrated here.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Transmission electron microscope images (TEM) for dendrimer D3a
reference_evidence_units.subject: D3a
reference_evidence_units.conditions: TEM images at different THF/water ratios, Fig. 24.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The paper's displayed morphology series is for D3a.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Do not present D3a particle sizes or micrographs as D5 measurements.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The blue emission band peaking at 446 and 477 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: PCTrPE
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Solid thin film; Fig. 3 and Table 1.
reference_evidence_units.statement: PCTrPE has blue vibronic emission together with a broader approximately 507 nm band, producing white emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The 509 nm single-band film result for PCTPE is a comparator and must not replace the PCTrPE spectrum.

reference_evidence_units.quote: with intra- and intermolecular energy transfer being totally restricted.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PCTrPE
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Interpretation of dual fluorescence in solid film and aggregate mixtures.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source interprets the two components as contributions of weakly coupled molecular fluorophores rather than efficient transfer to a single low-energy emitter.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The strong no-transfer wording is the authors' interpretation; it does not constitute measured zero transfer rate.

reference_evidence_units.quote: No delayed component can be observed
reference_evidence_units.subject: PCTrPE and PCTPE
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Transient PL in THF solutions and vacuum-deposited films; PCTrPE film lifetime reported as 3 ns.
reference_evidence_units.statement: No delayed component was detected; the source assigns the observed emission to prompt singlet decay.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Absence within the measurement window is not proof that no triplet population exists under any conditions.

reference_evidence_units.quote: PCTrPE in solutions with fw lower than 70%
reference_evidence_units.subject: PCTrPE
reference_evidence_units.conditions: THF/water titration, Fig. 3c.
reference_evidence_units.statement: An additional long-wavelength band appears near 70% water; at 99% water broad white emission has a reported yield of 16%.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Emission wavelength and relative bands depend on morphology and medium; the two observed components are not evidence by themselves for anti-Kasha emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: No obvious p–p interaction is observed in the crystal
reference_evidence_units.subject: PCTrPE crystal
reference_evidence_units.conditions: X-ray packing analysis, Fig. 4b.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Edge-to-face zigzag packing isolates PC planes and lacks obvious face-to-face pi stacking, which the source relates to reduced aggregation quenching.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Crystal packing is source-reported structural evidence, not confirmation of the inherited graph or proof that every film shares identical packing.

reference_evidence_units.quote: without any contribution from excimer and exciplex emission.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PCTrPE device
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Comparison of PL, EL and transport-layer spectra, Fig. 6.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors reject excimer/exciplex emission as the explanation for the white PCTrPE device emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This bounded source interpretation must not be inverted into a positive excimer label merely because there is a red band.

reference_evidence_units.quote: XRD patterns of the drop-cast films
reference_evidence_units.subject: PCTrPE and PCTPE films
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Drop-cast film XRD continued on physical page 6.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source identifies predominantly amorphous films, with packing context differing from the single-crystal analysis.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Do not silently treat single-crystal geometry as a measured atomistic structure of the amorphous films.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the emission maximum shifts considerably from 2.87 eV in ethanol to 2.63 eV in the MOF
reference_evidence_units.subject: ADB in solution and Zn-ADB SURMOF-2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Spectra from earlier experimental work reproduced/discussed in this computational study.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source reports a small absorption red shift and a larger emission red shift when ADB is incorporated into the MOF.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The experimental spectra originate in cited reference 51; they are not new measurements generated by this computational paper.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Both orbitals are largely localized on the central anthracene unit.
reference_evidence_units.subject: isolated ADB
reference_evidence_units.conditions: PBE0 calculations of the lowest singlet transition, Fig. 2 and Table 1.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The HOMO, LUMO and transition density are predominantly localized on the anthracene core, with weak solvent dependence.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Localized orbital character does not support assigning generic donor-acceptor ICT solely from terminal acid groups.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the optically weakly allowed Sb state comes to lie lowest in energy
reference_evidence_units.subject: anthracene model dimer
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Slip scan for simplified anthracene dimers modeled on the framework geometry.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Slip changes the ordering of bright and dark states; at the framework-like slip the lowest state is weakly allowed.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This simplified model is not the full ADB framework calculation; target-specific calculations below test the same explanation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the angle between the phenylene and anthracene planes is reduced from 81
reference_evidence_units.subject: ADB in Zn-SURMOF-2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Periodic PBE reference structure and PBE0-D3 cluster optimization.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Neighboring linkers induce conformational changes and greater conjugation relative to an isolated node-linker unit.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Fixed node positions and finite-cluster approximations constrain the geometry; no source SMILES adjudication is implied.

reference_evidence_units.quote: there are two competing effects regarding the change in the absorption spectrum
reference_evidence_units.subject: ADB in Zn-SURMOF-2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Full node-linker dimers/tetramers versus isolated units.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Conformational planarization red-shifts absorption while H-type coupling blue-shifts the strong transition; their combination explains the small net red shift.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: A red absorption shift alone would misidentify this system as purely J-type.

reference_evidence_units.quote: what counts for the emission characteristics according to Kasha’s rule
reference_evidence_units.subject: ADB in Zn-SURMOF-2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Excited-state optimized tetramer, Table 5.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Absorption is dominated by strongly allowed higher states whereas emission comes from weakly allowed S1. The source explicitly follows Kasha's rule.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Absorption into a higher state is not anti-Kasha emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: massive, excitation-induced conformational changes, as one would expect in classical excimers, do not play a role.
reference_evidence_units.subject: ADB in Zn-SURMOF-2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Comparison of ground- and excited-state geometry and coupling.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The newer analysis explains the red emission through slipped H-aggregate excitonic coupling rather than a classical strongly relaxed excimer.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The family still includes aggregate excitons; rejection of a classical excimer must not delete all aggregate-coupling support.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the particularly low oscillator strength of 0.06
reference_evidence_units.subject: ADB framework tetramer
reference_evidence_units.conditions: S1 emission calculation at relaxed geometry; comparison to previously reported overall lifetime.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The small calculated emission oscillator strength motivates a long radiative lifetime and a possible time-dependent spectral contribution from different local environments.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Overall lifetime around 4 ns is not the radiative lifetime. Sample inhomogeneity is a proposed explanation, not directly imaged here.

reference_evidence_units.quote: intramolecular charge transfer occurs from the electron-donating anthracene moiety to the electron-accepting aldehyde group.

reference_evidence_units.subject: 9-anthraldehyde aggregates

reference_evidence_units.quote: the hydrodynamic ones in the solution.

reference_evidence_units.statement: Keto S0-S1 gap becomes small near 60 degrees and crosses near 90 degrees; authors associate torsion-accessible CI with weak solution fluorescence.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The intersection point between the S0 and S1 states was found at the torsion angle of 60°
reference_evidence_units.subject: HPIP keto form
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Fully relaxed CASSCF(6,6)/ANO-S-MB exploration, continued from p.5.
reference_evidence_units.statement: A relaxed pathway locates an intersection around 60 degrees, about 19 kJ/mol downhill from the keto S1 minimum at 37.7 degrees.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Method differs from the constrained 90-degree crossing. The paper does not supply measured CI crossing dynamics.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Suppression of the efficient radiationless decay process via the S0/S1 CI allows emissive decay
reference_evidence_units.subject: HPIP
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Crystals with torsions below 6 degrees, frozen solution and polymer matrix.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Fixing a nearly planar geometry is proposed to prevent twisting toward CI and permit nanosecond keto S1 fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: RIM, environmental confinement and CI restriction describe overlapping levels of this same proposed pathway.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the S1-keto state can be regarded as an energy trap to inhibit exciton migration.
reference_evidence_units.subject: HPIP crystals
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Antiparallel stacked crystal pairs, approximately 3.4 angstrom spacing.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The low keto S1 energy and distinct keto/enol electronic structures are proposed to inhibit migration and excimer formation despite close stacking.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: An energetic rationale, not direct proof that all intermolecular coupling vanishes; similar solid/matrix photophysics is supporting evidence.

reference_evidence_units.quote: no phosphorescence was observed in the solid state or frozen solution at 77 K
reference_evidence_units.subject: HPIP
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Solid and frozen solution at 77 K.
reference_evidence_units.statement: No phosphorescence is reported; authors assign the proximity n-pi*/pi-pi* effect a minor role.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: A non-detection does not exclude every triplet population or arbitrarily weak phosphorescence.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the fluorescence color difference between the two crystal polymorphs
reference_evidence_units.subject: HPIP BG and Y crystals
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Comparison of experimental BG/Y energies with CASSCF, MS-CASPT2 and EOM-CCSD; Table 8 on p.6.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The calculations fail to reproduce the BG/Y color difference satisfactorily; larger calculations and environmental effects remain open.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: CI-based enhancement must not be represented as a solved quantitative model of polymorph color.

reference_evidence_units.quote: no drastic change in the dipole moment was observed upon the S1 or the S2 excitations.
reference_evidence_units.subject: HPIP enol; keto comparison
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Orbital and Mulliken analyses, Tables 4-5.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Enol excitation shows limited net CT; keto excitation involves intramolecular redistribution from phenol toward imidazopyridine.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Electronic redistribution is embedded in tautomer photophysics, not a separately established PET turn-on mechanism.

reference_evidence_units.quote: a major red emission band appears at 600 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: CF3-HTTH
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Pristine solid powder at room temperature; Fig. 1c, excitation 380 nm.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Normal/vibronic emission around 440-460 nm and tautomer emission around 520 nm coexist with a broad 600 nm band.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Band locations used for maxima and monitoring differ (e.g., 550/650 nm); do not treat every monitoring wavelength as a peak maximum.

reference_evidence_units.quote: disappears when CF3-HTTH is deposited as a thin film
reference_evidence_units.subject: CF3-HTTH
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Comparison of powder, solution, vapor-deposited quartz film and PMMA; PMMA result reported from SI.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The broad red band is absent in solution and deposited/dispersed films, supporting a packing-dependent intermolecular origin.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: SI PMMA data not inspected; absence of the band in these conditions does not mean all aggregate states are nonemissive.

reference_evidence_units.quote: CF3-MTTH with ESIPT reveals negligible excimer emission
reference_evidence_units.subject: CF3-MTTH and CF3-MTTM
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Methylated controls and crystal analysis, Fig. 1 and Table 1.
reference_evidence_units.statement: MTTH supports ESIPT but little excimer, while fully methylated MTTM can form an excimer without ESIPT. Packing and excited-state competition both matter.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Comparator behavior is not transferred to target. ESIPT is not a universal prerequisite for excimer formation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: a long rise component of 400 ps is obvious
reference_evidence_units.subject: CF3-HTTH
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Pristine powder, room temperature; 400 nm excitation; TCSPC monitoring 650 nm, Fig. 2a/Table 2 visually inspected.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Excimer-dominated red emission rises in about 400 ps and decays in about 2.4 ns; normal and tautomer signals have matching approximately 400 ps decays.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Observed 400 ps is a coupled kinetic time constant, not an independently measured elementary excimer-formation rate.

reference_evidence_units.quote: decay time of the normal emission (460 nm) of 3.9 ± 0.2 ps
reference_evidence_units.subject: CF3-HTTH
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Femtosecond up-conversion, 400 nm excitation, Fig. 2b.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Normal emission decay of 3.9 +/- 0.2 ps matches tautomer rise of 3.8 +/- 0.2 ps, followed by a longer decay.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Instrument response about 120 fs; fit uncertainty and reversible proton transfer must be retained.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The forward (kpt) and reverse (k−pt) ESIPT are fitted
reference_evidence_units.subject: CF3-HTTH
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Coupled N*, T*, E* rate-equation simulation; Eqs. 3-8 and methods p.8.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors fit forward/reverse ESIPT times of 4.6/26 ps and coupled 362 ps N*/T* decay/E* rise; reversible ESIPT channels population through N* to E*.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Model-dependent fits; kT is taken from CF3-MTTH. These are reported author simulations, not new calculations. Fig. 5 inset contains an apparent 362 ns typo unlike equations.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the emission spectra become similar to that of pristine powder
reference_evidence_units.subject: CF3-HTTH
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Crystal grinding at room temperature, Fig. 6 on p.7 visually inspected.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Grinding increases relative normal/tautomer contributions and makes the crystal spectrum resemble powder; vapor-deposited film lacks the excimer band.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Normalized spectra show relative spectral redistribution, not absolute integrated quantum-yield changes.

reference_evidence_units.quote: crystal surface has significantly more and narrower lifetime distribution at 1.5–1.7 ns
reference_evidence_units.subject: CF3-HTTH
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Two-photon microscopy, 800 nm excitation; surface vs approximately 6 micrometers depth, Fig. 7 visually inspected.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Crystal interior is more excimer-dominated; the surface shows larger 1.5-1.7 ns normal/tautomer components.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Three-exponential fitting and spatial resolution limit separation; surface spectra can still contain red contributions, so do not call the measured surface entirely excimer-free.

reference_evidence_units.quote: proper orientation of neighbor molecules facilitates the for- mation of excimer after fast equilibrium of ESIPT reaction.
reference_evidence_units.subject: CF3-HTTH
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Discussion of morphology and depth-resolved spectra.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors explain mechanochromism by different surface/interior packing that alters excimer formation after reversible ESIPT equilibration.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Bounded source model: not a generic RIM assignment and not demonstrated for every congener.

reference_evidence_units.quote: blue-shifted to 550 nm after addition of Zn2+
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPESB with zinc
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 1e-5 M in THF/water 1:1, excitation 365 nm; Figs. 4-5.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Zn2+ rapidly enhances fluorescence and shifts the weak approximately 600 nm band toward 550 nm, with a new approximately 490 nm absorption band; tested competing ions show only slight changes.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Selectivity is limited to tested ions and conditions; zinc response is not simply solvent-driven aggregation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The chelation effect will restrict the PET effect and prevent the ESIPT
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPESB with zinc
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Binding model supported by main-text accounts of Job plot, MS, NMR and FTIR, SI S15-S19.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors propose 1:1 Zn coordination involving phenolic oxygens and imine nitrogens; this suppresses PET, ESIPT and nonradiative decay to explain enhanced blue-shifted fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: All detailed binding controls are SI reported in main, not independently inspected. Zinc binding does not establish metal-centered or triplet emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: decrease of the HOMO-LUMO energy gap of zinc complex of TPESB
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPESB and zinc complex
reference_evidence_units.conditions: B3LYP/6-31G orbital comparison, Fig. 6.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Calculated complex gap is lower than free TPESB, used to rationalize the new absorption band.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Orbital gap alone does not prove an emissive CT state, PET rate or the observed blue shift.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Explicit aggregate-induced RIR interpretation is retained with its tentative language and indirect controls.

reference_mechanisms.label: PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Aggregate packing and matrix-dependent water access modulate emission; this is enabling environment, not a universal PEG-rigidification claim.

reference_mechanisms.label: HOST_GUEST_INTERACTION
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Under the frozen analyte-binding definition, zinc chelation changes target emission. This is molecular coordination, not macrocycle inclusion.

reference_mechanisms.label: ESIPT_PT

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET

source_documents.title: Constructing adaptive photosensitizers via supramolecular modification based on pillararene host−guest interactions

reference_evidence_units.quote: G has a small overlap between HOMO and LUMO
reference_evidence_units.subject: G
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Reported TD-DFT, Scheme 2.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Separated donor/acceptor orbitals and a calculated singlet-triplet gap of 0.2 eV are used to propose efficient ISC for ROS production.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No ISC rate was measured in the inspected text; reported calculation is not a new inference experiment.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the consumption of ABDA was calculated to be 4.5 nmol
reference_evidence_units.subject: G; Ce6 comparator
reference_evidence_units.conditions: G 30 micromolar, ABDA 5 nmol; white-light assay with probe photobleaching subtracted, Fig. 1a.
reference_evidence_units.statement: ABDA consumption is reported as 4.5 nmol with G in 140 s; comparator Ce6 gives 1.7 nmol in 300 s.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Different reported time points must be retained; ABDA consumption is not itself an absolute singlet-oxygen quantum yield.

reference_evidence_units.quote: about 0.4 nmol ABDA was consumed
reference_evidence_units.subject: G with WP5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: WP5 and G each 30 micromolar in aqueous medium, 5 min white-light irradiation.
reference_evidence_units.statement: WP5 complexation greatly reduces ROS-indicator consumption relative to G alone.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Fluorescence and ROS need separate comparisons; the complex and free guest are not interchangeable states.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The consumption of ABDA was calculated to be 2.2 nmol in 300 s
reference_evidence_units.subject: G with WP5/P5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Host and G each 30 micromolar, pH 5.0, Fig. 1a.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Acidification restores ROS-indicator consumption to 2.2 nmol in 300 s, consistent with partial switching on.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Do not equate this value with the 4.5 nmol/140 s free-G result. Cell viability used pH 6.0 rather than 5.0.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Negligible change in fluorescence was observed after addition of WP5
reference_evidence_units.subject: G and G/host controls
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Aqueous G 30 micromolar; WP5 30 micromolar; Fig. 2a-b.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Free G is weakly emissive; WP5 addition or acidification of G alone causes negligible fluorescence change, whereas acidification of G plus WP5 below pH 6 enhances emission strongly.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The abstract's generic quenching wording must not obscure that free G already has weak aqueous fluorescence.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the alkyl chain was threaded into the cavity of WP5.
reference_evidence_units.subject: G with WP5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 1H NMR and NOE evidence reported from SI S10-S12.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Alkyl/pyridinium shifts and alkyl-host NOEs are interpreted as threading with carboxylate-pyridinium electrostatics, forming a pseudorotaxane.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: SI not inspected; detailed binding geometry remains a source-supported interpretation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Then photoinduced electron transfer (PET) happened between WP5 and G
reference_evidence_units.subject: G with WP5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Neutral aqueous host-guest complex; source cites SI S13.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors invoke host-guest PET to suppress ROS generation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No direction, rate or direct kinetic evidence is established by the inspected main text; do not infer PET from fluorescence alone.

reference_evidence_units.quote: only NOE signals between protons Ha1,a2 on the endmost pyridinium unit of G and proton H1 on P5 were observed
reference_evidence_units.subject: G with protonated P5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: pH 5.0; SI S15/S16-S17 discussed in main text.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors interpret acidification as movement of protonated host to the terminal pyridinium, not complete host dissociation. Hydrophobic shielding leads to G/P5 coprecipitation and fluorescence enhancement; distance from TPE core permits ROS recovery.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: SI not inspected; proposed shuttling model is not a crystal structure of this target complex. Cited analogous crystal structure is background.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the self-assemblies were changed to large aggregates
reference_evidence_units.subject: G and host-dependent assemblies
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Main-text report of TEM SI S18: G, G/WP5 and acidic G/WP5.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Reported morphology changes from free-G vesicles to tiny particles with WP5, then large aggregates at pH 5.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: TEM itself not inspected; free-G vesicles complicate describing all aqueous G as exclusively molecularly dissolved.

reference_mechanisms.label: PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Host-dependent coprecipitation and aggregate morphology underpin the fluorescence switch; it does not prove a specific internal RIM coordinate.

reference_mechanisms.label: HOST_GUEST_INTERACTION
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Central pH-dependent host binding/shuttling interpretation explains switching; not assumed host release.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The source invokes donor-acceptor orbital separation to reduce the singlet-triplet gap. This is bounded electronic-structure support, not measured TICT kinetics.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Explicit host-guest PET suppression of photosensitization and recovery after proposed relocation is retained with limited direct evidence.

reference_mechanisms.label: TRIPLET_METAL_ENERGY_TRANSFER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Source links small computed singlet-triplet gap and ISC to ROS photosensitization. This is a photosensitizer pathway, not phosphorescence or metal emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: almost all the pyridinium groups resided in the cavities of CB[8]
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-2EP with CB[8]
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 1H NMR titration in D2O, guest 0.2 mM; Fig. 1 p.7.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Pyridinium HA-F signals become almost invisible above one equivalent CB[8], whereas HG-I remain with a small upfield shift; authors infer near-complete arm inclusion and a linear assembly.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Peak disappearance alone does not quantitatively establish complete occupancy; linear topology is an author model.

reference_evidence_units.quote: their largest absorbance peaks had different degrees of red-shift.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-2EP with CB[8]
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Ultrapure water, guest 30 micromolar, guest:CB[8] 1:1; Fig. 2A p.9.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Target absorption maximum shifts from 375 to 420 nm after CB[8] assembly.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Absorption shifts are target-specific; electrostatic perturbation does not alone establish ICT, an exciton or an excimer.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The UV/Vis absorption spectra (A) and fluorescence spectra (B)
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-2EP with and without CB[8]
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Fig. 2B-C visually inspected; ultrapure water, guest 30 micromolar; ratio 1:1. Absolute PL yield method on pp.18-19.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The target's PL intensity increases and blue-shifts on complexation; Fig. 2C gives quantum yield 0.9% to 1.2%.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Values are read from the displayed target-specific table, not inferred from intensity scaling. No emission lifetime or separated rate constants are supplied.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the intramolecular motion in the bulk assembly could be further restricted.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-2EP, TPE-3EP and TPE-4EP CB[8] assemblies
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Aqueous host-induced assembly; p.8 photophysical discussion.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors propose that shared CB[8] cavities, bulky host and linked neighboring molecules restrict intramolecular motions, explaining fluorescence enhancement.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: An explicit series interpretation including the target, not independently measured molecular motion. It does not imply equal occupancy or enhancement across the series.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the hydrophobic cavity of CB[8] had a low-polarity microenvironment
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-EP series including TPE-2EP
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Blue shifts of the host-bound aqueous assemblies, Fig. 2B.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors attribute blue-shifted emission to a lower-polarity cavity environment.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Retain this polarity interpretation without upgrading it to experimentally established ICT/TICT; the paper does not explicitly resolve a CT excited state.

reference_evidence_units.quote: By calculating the quantitative data, the Ka between three kinds of AIE molecules and CB[8]
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-2EP with CB[8]
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Fluorescence titrations reported from SI S2; methods p.19 use 25 micromolar guest; excitation 375 nm.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The target's reported association constant is 7.15e6, assigned in the stated 2EP/3EP/4EP sequence.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: SI fit equations/uncertainties and the dimensional convention were not inspected; do not overinterpret a simple binding constant for a multivalent assembly.

reference_evidence_units.quote: TPE-2EP@CB[8] was about 200- 250 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-2EP@CB[8]
reference_evidence_units.conditions: SEM and cryo-TEM discussion, Fig. 3; 30 micromolar samples.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source reports target assemblies as roughly spherical, about 200-250 nm.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Morphology is reported from the main text; it is not molecular-resolution packing or proof of identical aggregation in cells.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the enhancement of fluorescence intensity was the effect of the accumulation of assemblies.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-2EP@CB[8] in cells
reference_evidence_units.conditions: SV-HUC-1 and T24 cells, 30 micromolar assembly; time-dependent flow cytometry, Fig. 5.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors attribute increasing cell fluorescence to uptake/accumulation. TPE-2EP assemblies give the largest fluorescence response, with membrane and intracellular staining.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Do not assign all cellular signal increase to per-molecule photophysical turn-on; size/shape-driven uptake is an author interpretation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: it was hardly observed the fluorescence signals of AIE supramolecular assemblies in cells
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-EP series including TPE-2EP
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Low-temperature co-staining control at 4 C versus 37 C; 20 min; Fig. 4 and SI S6-S7 discussed.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Assembly fluorescence in cells is strongly reduced at 4 C while tracker signal remains; authors use this to support active uptake.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Temperature inhibition is not a unique proof of a particular endocytosis pathway; SI controls not inspected.

reference_mechanisms.rationale: Authors explicitly propose CB[8]- and assembly-imposed RIM, supported indirectly by optical enhancement rather than direct torsional measurements.

reference_mechanisms.label: PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Cavity confinement and linked supramolecular assemblies are the enabling environment for RIM; overlapping mechanisms, not independent proof.

reference_mechanisms.label: HOST_GUEST_INTERACTION
reference_mechanisms.rationale: NMR and optical titrations support target-specific CB[8] association and changed emission; occupancy limitations are retained.

reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE–DBA

reference_evidence_units.limitations: Name/function mapping only; molecular graph, E/Z configuration and legacy SMILES remain unverified. DBA is reported as an E/Z mixture.

reference_evidence_units.quote: When the fW reaches 90%, the system becomes highly emissive
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE–DBA
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 10 micromolar THF/water, excitation 360 nm; Fig. 1 visually inspected.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the protonated amines are capable of recognizing the crown ethers

reference_evidence_units.conditions: Equimolar TPE-DBA/TPE-DDBC in THF; acid/base switching, Fig. 2A.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Protonation permits ammonium-crown binding; base-induced deionization is proposed to dissociate the supramolecular assembly.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Ground-state protonation is not ESIPT. Detailed stoichiometry/association kinetics are not established by the inspected main text.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The non-covalent inter- action of the host will lock on the rotations of benzylamino groups
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE–DBA in the two-component assembly
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Acidified equimolar mixture; source's target-specific RIR explanation.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors propose crown binding to protonated benzylamino groups locks rotations coupled to the TPE phenyls, turning on emission of the DBA guest.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The fluorescent mixture was not spectrally decomposed into separate guest and host contributions; retain the author's proposed attribution, not measured component fractions.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The FL ‘‘turn-on/turn-off’’ behaviours are reversible
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE–DBA with complementary building block
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Each building block 5e-4 M in THF, 1:1; HCl/NaOH aqueous stocks 1 M; excitation 360 nm; Fig. 2B-C inspected.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Acid produces a fluorescent white precipitate after 10 min sonication; base removes precipitate and fluorescence. Three cycles are shown.

reference_evidence_units.quote: such low water fraction cannot lead to the aggregation of TPE–DBA and TPE–DDBC.

reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors argue the initial turn-on is from host-guest-induced insoluble assembly, not water alone.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This is a water-fraction control, not a complete exclusion of ionic strength, counterion or protonation-related contributions.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the emission became stronger and the emission peak blue-shifted after every cycle.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE–DBA in cyclic mixture assemblies
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Three acid/base cycles, Fig. 2B-C and Fig. 3.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors associate stepwise intensity increases with tighter packing as water accumulates, and blue shifts with increased structural order/twisting.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The cycle is reversible in on/off behavior but not identical in brightness. Packing/twisting explanation is proposed, not molecularly resolved.

reference_evidence_units.quote: microscopic wires with diameters of about 100 nm

reference_evidence_units.limitations: SEM samples are prepared solids; morphology does not by itself quantify internal rotation or resolve each component.

reference_evidence_units.conditions: Discussion of chloride and alternative anions.

reference_evidence_units.limitations: Alternative counterions are a proposal, not experiments inspected here; retain this limitation on the HCl-driven model.

source_documents.title: Aggregation-Induced Emission (AIE)-Active Fluorescent Probes with Multi-Binding Sites toward ATP Sensing and the Live Cell Imaging

reference_evidence_units.quote: TPA-PPA-2 was an orange solid
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPA-PPA-2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Named synthesis section; Scheme 1 p.4.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source explicitly distinguishes TPA-PPA-2 from the one- and three-arm congeners and reports its isolation and NMR characterization.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Identity is followed by name/designation only; no chemical graph or legacy SMILES confirmation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The HOMO orbital is mostly dominated in the TPA cores
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPA-PP/TPA-PPA series including TPA-PPA-2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Gaussian09 OPT/FREQ/B3LYP/6-31G*; Fig. 2.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors report HOMO density on TPA and LUMO on pyridinium acceptors, interpreted as ICT tendency for all four probes.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The printed very small gaps labeled eV are questionable in magnitude/unit convention; no numerical gap is adopted or silently corrected.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the fluorescence property is greatly affected by the solvent polarity
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPA-PPA-2 within four-probe series
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Solvent study, 20 micromolar, Fig. 3; target excitation 437 nm.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors interpret solvent-dependent emission as probably ICT-related; the target is included in the measured series.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Solvent polarity changes can also change hydrogen bonding and aggregation. No TICT geometry or time-resolved CT formation is established.

reference_evidence_units.quote: their fluorescence lifetimes were lengthened to 4.9, 2.9, 4.3 and 4.9 nanoseconds, respectively.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPA-PPA-2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Fig. 4, target third in TPA-PP/PPA-1/PPA-2/PPA-3 sequence.
reference_evidence_units.statement: TPA-PPA-2 has a reported fluorescence lifetime of 4.3 ns.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Inspected caption does not specify the solvent/ATP condition or a before-after pair; do not call 4.3 ns an ATP-induced lifetime increase.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Plots of maximum emission intensity (I/I0) of TPA-PP, TPA- PPA-1, TPA-PPA-2, TPA-PPA-3 with the addition of ATP.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPA-PPA-2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 20 micromolar probe, aqueous 2 vol% DMSO, pH 7.0; ATP 10-300 micromolar, Fig. 5 visually inspected.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The target-specific blue-triangle curve increases with added ATP, intermediate between PPA-1 and PPA-3 over the plotted range.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No comparator detection limit, quantum-yield enhancement or selectivity is assigned to PPA-2; plotted intensity response alone does not prove a binding geometry.

reference_evidence_units.quote: possibly due to the synergistic effect of electrostaticat traction and covalent bonds formation
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPA-PPA series including TPA-PPA-2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: ATP-dependent absorption/emission; PP/PPA-1 comparison and multi-binding-site rationale.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors propose combined pyridinium-phosphate electrostatics and boronic-acid/cis-diol bonding for ATP recognition; extra binding sites are proposed to improve response.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Detailed comparator comparison is PP versus PPA-1 and strongest claims concern PPA-3. The PPA-2 binding mode is a bounded series interpretation, not independently resolved stoichiometry.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Plots of maximum emission intensity of TPA-PP, TPA-PPA-1, TPA-PPA-2, TPA-PPA-3
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPA-PPA-2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Fig. 6 visually inspected; 20 micromolar in glycerol/methanol mixtures, glycerol fraction up to 0.95.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The separately labeled PPA-2 blue-triangle curve rises substantially at high glycerol fraction, so viscosity response is observed for this target and not only PPA-3.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Changing glycerol content also changes solvent properties. The photograph inset and quoted approximately fivefold result in the prose concern PPA-3, not PPA-2.

reference_evidence_units.quote: restriction of intramolecular rotations (RIR), blocking the non-radiative pathway
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPA probe series including TPA-PPA-2; detailed ATP model illustrated by PPA-3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Interpretation motivating the four-probe glycerol test, followed by PPA-3-specific ATP model.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors invoke RIR to explain viscosity-enhanced emission, and propose that multi-site ATP association also restricts motion.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: PPA-2 has its own viscosity curve, but the proposed ATP-induced viscosity increase is not independently measured for PPA-2; do not equate bulk viscosity with confirmed molecular binding geometry.

reference_evidence_units.quote: we can hard to say that these new developed sensors are exactly ATP-specific in the mammalian cells.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPA probe series including TPA-PPA-2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: HepG-2 imaging and DAPI comparisons; Figs. 8-9.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors explicitly stop short of assigning cellular staining specifically to ATP, noting charge-mediated uptake and interactions with other bioanalytes.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Cell imaging does not validate in-cell ATP specificity. Prose gives 30 min while Fig. 8 and methods indicate 60 min/1 h.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the emission spectrum of TPA- PPA-3 changed negligibly upon the addition of ADP, AMP, and other anions
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPA-PPA-3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 20 micromolar PPA-3, 100 micromolar analytes; Fig. 7.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Detailed ATP-versus-ADP/AMP selectivity testing is presented for PPA-3.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This is not a target-specific PPA-2 selectivity demonstration. Likewise, the 0.3 ppm detection limit and approximately 26-fold quantum-yield change in p.5 belong to PPA-3.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Target-specific viscosity response plus the source's explicit RIR interpretation supports bounded RIR; ATP-induced restriction is more tentative than the solvent test.

reference_mechanisms.label: HOST_GUEST_INTERACTION
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Under the frozen analyte-binding definition, ATP recognition is proposed to alter emission via multi-site association. This is a probe/analyte interaction, not macrocycle inclusion; PPA-2 geometry remains unverified.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Preserve the source's calculated donor-acceptor separation and probable ICT interpretation of solvent dependence, without adopting suspect gap units or asserting TICT.

mechanism_decisions.label: RIM_RIR_RIV

reference_evidence_units.quote: In water the dye has an emission maximum around 486 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMN-Bu
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Aqueous dye, 10 micromolar; surfactant titrations at near-neutral pH.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The aqueous aggregate emission is near 486 nm. CTAB addition produces a longer-wavelength band near 600 nm above the micellar regime.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The spectral change is observed; assignment to monomers and aggregates requires the source comparisons below.

reference_evidence_units.quote: A clear isoemissive point at 554 nm shows a clear transformation
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMN-Bu with CTAB
reference_evidence_units.conditions: CTAB titration; aqueous dye 10 micromolar.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors interpret the isoemissive point and opposite changes in the two bands as aggregate-to-monomer conversion.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: An isoemissive point is consistent with conversion but does not independently prove aggregate geometry.

reference_evidence_units.quote: rotational correlation time increases to 0.85 ns
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMN-Bu in CTAB micelles
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Time-resolved anisotropy under CTAB micellar conditions.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The micelle-associated dye has a reported rotational correlation time of 0.85 ns.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Whole-body rotational reorientation is not direct measurement of an intramolecular torsional barrier.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Here we required more than 4 mM of Tween-20 to complete the deaggregation process
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMN-Bu with Tween-20
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Nonionic Tween-20 titration in water.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Complete deaggregation requires more than 4 mM Tween-20, substantially above the stated approximately 0.06 mM CMC.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Do not infer that the dye's transition locates the CMC equally well for every surfactant.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This can be explained by the presence of high dipole moment of DMN-Bu due to an intramolecular charge transfer nature of the dye.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMN-Bu in surfactant environments
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Comparison of monomer emission and lifetime in ionic and nonionic micelles.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors invoke the dye's ICT character to explain sensitivity to the polarity of different micellar environments.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This is an ICT interpretation, not a demonstrated twisted CT geometry or an independent electron-transfer reaction.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Since the aggregates are blue shifted with respect to the monomers in the case of both ionic as well as non-ionic surfactants, we confirm the existence of H-aggregates of DMN-Bu molecules in water.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMN-Bu
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Excitation spectra before and after surfactant-induced deaggregation.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source assigns aqueous dye aggregates as H-aggregates from their blue-shifted spectra relative to monomers.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: A source-supported spectral assignment, not crystal-resolved packing or definitive exciton geometry.

reference_evidence_units.quote: cyclodextrin is too small to accommodate any napthalimide dye, but it has a good affinity towards SDS.
reference_evidence_units.subject: alpha-cyclodextrin, SDS and DMN-Bu
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Alpha-cyclodextrin is added to the previously deaggregated dye-SDS solution.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The proposed host-guest step captures SDS rather than inserting DMN-Bu into the cyclodextrin cavity.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Host binding is system-mediated and involves a different guest. This must not become a direct dye-inclusion claim.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the emission maxima at 620 nm start to decrease
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMN-Bu in SDS with added alpha-cyclodextrin
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Titration with alpha-cyclodextrin; changes begin near 2 mM.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The 620 nm band decreases and a band near 470 nm grows; the source also reports a 13 nm blue shift of excitation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Consistent with restored dye aggregation through micelle disruption, not proof of direct dye-host inclusion.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Plot of the fluorescence intensity of 10 μM DMN-Bu with varying concentration
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMN-Bu with alpha-cyclodextrin alone
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Embedded SI Fig. S6, water without SDS; 0, 2, 6 and 10.8 mM alpha-cyclodextrin.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The plotted spectra retain a similar shape and show a modest intensity decrease rather than the large spectral conversion seen with SDS present.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Figure visually inspected. The effect is small relative to the SDS-mediated conversion, not literally zero; no digitized intensity or binding constant is inferred.

reference_evidence_units.quote: corresponding to an approximate 84-fold enhancement in emission intensity
reference_evidence_units.subject: ALITPE with sulfated beta-cyclodextrin (SCD)
