reference_evidence_units.subject: ALITPE with SCD
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Interpretation of the concentration-dependent fluorescence and charge-neutralized assemblies.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors connect oppositely charged host-guest association, aggregation and restriction of ALITPE rotation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The rotation mechanism is inferred, not a directly measured torsional potential.

reference_evidence_units.quote: notably slow decay of the complex
reference_evidence_units.subject: ALITPE with SCD
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Time-resolved anisotropy at 31.3 micromolar ALITPE and 6.5 micromolar SCD, Fig. 5.
reference_evidence_units.statement: An anisotropy fit gives rotational correlation time around 2.8 ns and residual anisotropy around 0.15; the source also reports DLS aggregates around 150 nm.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Whole-assembly rotation is not internal phenyl rotation. DLS is reported in the main text but underlying SI Fig. S3 is unavailable.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the inefficiency of unsubstituted βCD molecules in inducing the aggregation of ALITPE molecules
reference_evidence_units.subject: ALITPE with native beta-cyclodextrin versus SCD
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Native-host control, Fig. 6, compared with sulfated host.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The weak response with native beta-cyclodextrin supports an important role for the charged sulfate groups rather than a generic cyclodextrin cavity.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: A comparative interpretation of fluorescence, not an atomically resolved binding measurement.

reference_evidence_units.quote: it takes around 80 mM of NaCl to reduce the fluorescence intensity of this supramolecular aggregate until it reaches the emission level of the free dye in water
reference_evidence_units.subject: ALITPE with SCD under salt titration
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 31.3 micromolar ALITPE and 6.5 micromolar SCD; NaCl additions, Fig. 7-9.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Increasing salt reduces fluorescence towards the free-dye level near 80 mM. Absorption/scattering and lifetime trends support loss of the emitting assemblies.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Salt tolerance is finite. Do not turn a relative tolerance comparison into a claim that salt leaves the assembly unaffected.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the absorption spectra revealed an increment in the long-wavelength offset
reference_evidence_units.subject: ALITPE with SCD under heating
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 31.3 micromolar ALITPE and 6.5 micromolar SCD; Figs. 11-13, temperature-dependent spectra and lifetimes.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Heating reduces emission and lifetime while increasing the long-wavelength absorption offset. The displayed curves were checked; the source interprets the offset as increased turbidity/aggregation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Unlike the salt and excess-host responses, thermal quenching is not assigned to aggregate disassembly. Scattering is a proxy for aggregation, not a quantitative aggregate count.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Since the temperature increase does not lead to the dissociation
reference_evidence_units.subject: ALITPE with SCD under heating
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Interpretation of simultaneous temperature-dependent absorption, fluorescence and lifetime measurements.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors attribute thermal quenching to increased nonradiative molecular motion while aggregates remain present.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The claim of a sole cause is the authors' interpretation; no independent separation of radiative and nonradiative rates is provided here.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The Autodock Vina was used to perform molecular docking calculations.
reference_evidence_units.subject: ALITPE and SCD
reference_evidence_units.conditions: PM3-optimized inputs, docking with a 40 angstrom cubic search box, exhaustiveness 1000; successive docking builds 1:1 and 2:1 models.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Docking explores plausible host-guest arrangements and interactions.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Selected geometries are model hypotheses, not experimental determination of stoichiometry, cavity occupancy or aggregate morphology.

reference_evidence_units.quote: stabilize ALITPE on the surface of SCD
reference_evidence_units.subject: ALITPE and SCD
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Interpretation of docking in Fig. 15 and the host/salt experiments.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source describes electrostatic and other noncovalent contacts at the SCD surface.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Do not equate surface association with verified cavity inclusion. Docked pi contacts alone do not establish H/J excitons or excimer emission.

reference_evidence_units.statement: The source reports no significant turn-on for free ALITPE under the tested perturbations, supporting a role for SCD.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Underlying control plots are unavailable. This is not a statement that free-dye fluorescence is invariant under every possible condition.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the further rotation of the azetidine group is energetically unfavorable on the S1 and S2 PESs.
reference_evidence_units.subject: AZE-Ph-BDP
reference_evidence_units.conditions: THF energy scans of both candidate rotation coordinates.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Azetidine remains aligned with the phenyl group; its further rotation is unfavorable.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Coordinate assignment is model-dependent; Figure 6b-c visually inspected.

reference_evidence_units.quote: resulting in a negligible oscillator strength (f = 0.00; Figure 6c).
reference_evidence_units.subject: AZE-Ph-BDP
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Computed lowest singlet perpendicular conformation in THF.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The fully separated TICT configuration is calculated to be dark.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Calculated oscillator strength is not an experimentally determined radiative rate; S2 in the scan is not evidence of S2 emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: AZE-Ph-BDP is emissive only in hexane (Φ = 0.36; Figure 6d).
reference_evidence_units.subject: AZE-Ph-BDP
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Solvent comparison; Figure 6d visually inspected.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Hexane quantum yield is 0.36; tested polar solvents have negligible yield.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Only the tested solvent set is covered, not all possible environments.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the fluorescence of AZE-Ph-BDP greatly intensifies in highly viscous solvents.
reference_evidence_units.subject: AZE-Ph-BDP
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Ethanol/glycerol volume-ratio series, Figure 6e.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Increasing the glycerol-rich viscous fraction strongly enhances fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Viscosity and solvent composition co-vary; this is not an isolated torsion-rate measurement.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The molecular aggregates effectively inhibit TICT rotations.
reference_evidence_units.subject: AZE-Ph-BDP
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Dioxane/water aggregation series, Figure 6f.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors assign aggregation turn-on to restriction of TICT rotations.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: A bounded source interpretation supported by solvent, viscosity and calculation comparisons, not definitive exclusion of other mechanisms.

reference_evidence_units.quote: we observed a great enhancement of emission intensities, up to ~27 times.
reference_evidence_units.subject: AZE-Ph-BDP
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Dioxane/water series; main Figure 6f.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Aggregation produces reported fluorescence enhancement up to about 27-fold.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The fold change is relative intensity, not a quantum yield; aggregate molecular packing is not resolved.

reference_evidence_units.quote: shows bright fluorescence in the solid state (Φ = 0.11; Figure S49).
reference_evidence_units.subject: AZE-Ph-BDP
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Solid-state result reported in main text with SI reference.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Solid quantum yield is reported as 0.11.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Figure S49 itself was not inspected.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the highly emissive LE state of Ph-BDP remains the most stable singlet excited state on a flat PES
reference_evidence_units.subject: Ph-BDP
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Parent BODIPY model, Figure 6b-c.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Parent Ph-BDP provides the bright LE comparator for the designed dark TICT monomer.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Do not transfer the parent's emissive state or quantum yield to AZE-Ph-BDP.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the rotation barriers and driving energies of P4 (ERB = 0.38 and EDE = -0.14 eV) and P5 (ERB = 0.27 and EDE = -0.24 eV) are larger than that of P2 (ERB = 0.23 and EDE = -0.36 eV)
reference_evidence_units.subject: P2, P4 and P5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: CAM-B3LYP/cLR-SMD in water; Figure 4d.
reference_evidence_units.statement: P2 has a 0.23 eV N-TICT barrier and -0.36 eV driving energy; P4 has 0.38 and -0.14 eV, predicting stronger resistance in P4.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Target-specific numbers are separated; no claim that P4 entirely prevents TICT.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the quantum yields of P4 (Φ = 0.38) and P5 (Φ = 0.33) are about twice than that of P2 (Φ = 0.17)
reference_evidence_units.subject: P2, P4 and P5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: PBS solution; Figure 4e visually inspected.
reference_evidence_units.statement: PBS quantum yield is 0.17 for P2, versus P4's 0.38.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Comparative brightness improvement is not an aggregation experiment.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the relative fluorescence intensity of P2 and P4 gradually increases when the water/glycerol ratio changed from 10/0 to 2/8.
reference_evidence_units.subject: P2 and P4
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Water/glycerol volume ratio 10/0 to 2/8; Figure 4f-g.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Both compounds brighten as glycerol increases.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Polarity changes together with viscosity; donor strength similarity is a control argument, not exact invariance of all solvent interactions.

reference_evidence_units.quote: P2 and P4 exhibit comparable quantum yield (Φ = 0.48 vs. 0.55) when the volume fraction of glycerol rises to 80%.
reference_evidence_units.subject: P2 and P4
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 80 vol% glycerol in water; Figure 4g.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The reported yields converge to P2 0.48 and P4 0.55.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Do not assign the comparator's yield to target; neither yield reaches unity.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the enhancement of fluorescence intensities of P2 and P4 can be attributed to TICT inhibition as glycerol is significantly more viscous and less polar than water is.
reference_evidence_units.subject: P2 and P4
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Water/glycerol solvent comparison.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors attribute enhancement to suppression of TICT in more viscous, less polar medium.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Restriction and polarity stabilization effects are not experimentally separated.

reference_evidence_units.quote: We thus attributed the short lifetime (τ1 = 79 ps) to the TICT state
reference_evidence_units.subject: P2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Transient absorption in PBS; Figure 4h-i.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors assign P2's short 79 ps ESA component to TICT and the approximately 0.92-0.94 ns components to emissive ICT.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Transient kinetic assignment is interpretive; comparison with charge-separated states is not direct geometric observation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the quantum yields of both P2 and P4 increased substantially (Table S2).
reference_evidence_units.subject: P2 and P4
reference_evidence_units.conditions: DMSO replaces water/glycerol to reduce hydrogen bonding around oxygen.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors report additional quantum-yield improvement in DMSO and retain hydrogen-bond quenching as a contributor.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: SI Table S2 was not inspected; no numeric DMSO yield is supplied here and no ESIPT is inferred.

reference_evidence_units.quote: While P4 is also prone to the TICT formation, it exhibited much stronger “TICT resistance”.
reference_evidence_units.subject: P2 and P4
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Combined viscosity, PBS and computed comparisons.
reference_evidence_units.statement: P4 has partial, not complete, TICT resistance relative to P2.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Neither compound's fluorescence is attributed solely to one pathway; hydrogen-bond quenching remains.

reference_mechanisms.rationale: The source assigns nonemissive N-TICT competing with emissive ICT in water, with P4 more resistant than P2.

reference_evidence_units.quote: HTI 3 serves as a control compound, which bears the same electron-rich stilbene part as 1, yet is not pretwisted in the ground state and thus does not undergo TICT formation in any solvent.
reference_evidence_units.subject: HTI Z-3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Planar comparator versus pretwisted HTI Z-1 and Z-2.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source uses non-pretwisted Z-3 as a negative TICT control.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The claim applies to solvents tested and is not evidence of aggregation or RIM turn-on in Z-1.

reference_evidence_units.quote: HTI Z-1 was dissolved in dCH, dDCM, and dDMSO
reference_evidence_units.subject: HTI Z-1
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Transient IR; 1.0-2.5 mg/mL deuterated solvents; pump 460-500 nm, magic-angle setup.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Z-1 was studied across apolar and polar solvents, with optical preparation of the Z state.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Concentration is the stated experimental range, not a solvent-specific concentration.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Z-1 and Z-2 show no spectral evolution of the initial excited-state spectrum toward new excited-state species in the apolar solvent dCH.
reference_evidence_units.subject: HTI Z-1 and Z-2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Apolar deuterated cyclohexane; time-resolved IR.
reference_evidence_units.statement: No evolution into a new excited-state spectral species is detected in dCH; decay and E photoproduct formation are reported.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No aggregation series is present; lack of TICT is condition-specific.

reference_evidence_units.quote: 210 ps for Z-1 and 32 ps for Z-2 in dDCM.
reference_evidence_units.subject: HTI Z-1 and Z-2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Global IR kinetic analysis in dDCM; Figure 3 visually inspected.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Reported TICT decay is about 210 ps for Z-1, versus about 32 ps for Z-2.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: These are different compounds, not interchangeable lifetimes; values are rounded in prose.

reference_evidence_units.quote: For Z-1, in dDCM (see Figure 3a,c), the C−O band shows a qualitatively similar behavior
reference_evidence_units.subject: HTI Z-1
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Transient IR band near 1515 cm-1 in dDCM.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The main text reports about 5 cm-1 shift with about 3 ps time constant, and amplitude maximum after about 30 ps.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Assignment is analogous to Z-2 rather than independently calculated for Z-1.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Kinetic Data Describing the Excited-State Processes for HTIs Z-1, Z-2, and Z-3 in Diﬀerent Solvents
reference_evidence_units.subject: HTI Z-1
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Table 2 visually inspected; colored time-constant assignments.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Table 2 gives Z-1 TICT lifetimes of 210.6 ps in dDCM and 17.8 ps in dDMSO; shift-time entries are 2.8 and 1.9 ps, respectively.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Caption anchors the visually read table; dCH 11.9 ps component is not marked TICT. The table header labels the shift column cm-1 although prose describes its entries as time constants; unit ambiguity retained.

reference_evidence_units.quote: We only focused on the Z-2 derivative as TICT forming species and neglected Z-1 in the calculations
reference_evidence_units.subject: HTI Z-2 and Z-3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: CASSCF/CASPT2 reaction pathways and TDDFT marker-band calculations.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The computational conical-intersection pathways and quantitative dipoles belong to Z-2/Z-3, not target Z-1.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No Z-1 CI geometry, dipole magnitude or state energy is transferred.

reference_evidence_units.quote: identification of the C−O marker band was not corroborated by quantum chemical calculations
reference_evidence_units.subject: HTI Z-1
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Final discussion of marker assignment.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source acknowledges that full Z-1 transient band assignment was not possible and assumes analogous behavior to Z-2.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This explicit uncertainty bounds the otherwise supported TICT interpretation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Solvent relaxation induced by the significant change in the dipole of the molecule for the TICT state could also contribute to the spectral shift
reference_evidence_units.subject: TICT-forming HTI derivatives
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Discussion of picosecond spectral shifts in polar solvents.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors retain solvent relaxation as a possible contributor to the evolving IR shift.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The shift is not treated as a uniquely geometric measure.

reference_evidence_units.quote: 1-Crys.(G) (quantum yield 17% and lifetime 1.24 ns) and 1-Crys.(YG) (quantum yield 13% and lifetime 1.15 ns)

reference_evidence_units.statement: G and YG have QY/lifetime 17%/1.24 ns and 13%/1.15 ns; peaks 521 and 540 nm.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Crystal measurements, not aqueous aggregate QY; no separate rate mechanism inferred.

reference_evidence_units.quote: intramolecular hydrogen bonds from the salicylaldimine, which provided a structural basis for ESIPT process, were observed for both of the two polymorphs.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 1 polymorphs
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Single-crystal X-ray Fig. 3.
reference_evidence_units.statement: H bonds are invoked as structural basis for ESIPT.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Ground-state structures do not demonstrate excited-state proton motion.

reference_evidence_units.quote: molecules in polymorph 1-Crys.(YG) packed in a much tighter mode, resulting in the fluorescence in a relative longer wavelength range.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 1 polymorphs
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Figs. 3-4, Table 1.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Tighter YG packing is proposed to explain redder emission; interplane spacing is smaller.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Fig. 4/Table 1 visually inspected. Prose says larger YG angles, but table angles are smaller; inconsistency not silently corrected.

reference_evidence_units.quote: they both existed as crystallines rather than amorphous powders
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 1 powders
reference_evidence_units.conditions: PXRD after synthesis or THF evaporation, Fig. 6.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Both powder states are crystalline, matching their crystal polymorphs.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Not merely an amorphous/crystalline transition; no raw refinement inspected.

reference_evidence_units.quote: upon repeated thermal cycles, the emission peak of 1 shifted between 522 and 541 nm as expected.

reference_evidence_units.conditions: 231 C annealing; 236 C melting followed by cooling; Fig. 8.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Repeated thermal treatment switches emission between 522 and 541 nm.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Detailed thermal-treatment PXRD and stability plots in SI were not inspected.

reference_evidence_units.quote: no solvent molecules were identied in the crystal lattice.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMIM polymorphs
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Diethyl ether vapor diffusion into chloroform; green crystals first, orange needles after days.
reference_evidence_units.statement: X-ray analysis finds no lattice solvent; green and orange forms have different packing and molecular conformers.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Not a solvent inclusion mechanism; kinetic versus thermodynamic preference is an author interpretation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: molecules in G-DMIM do not show this form of stacking.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMIM polymorphs
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Fig. 2 crystal packing; O-DMIM naphthalimide separation 3.73-3.75 angstrom.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Face-to-face naphthalimide stacking occurs in orange but not green crystals.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Packing does not on its own establish an excimer.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the HOMO clearly resides on the N,N-dimethylaniline group while the LUMO is localised on the naphthalimide subunit
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMIM
reference_evidence_units.conditions: DFT B3LYP/6-311G+(3df), cyclohexane continuum.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Computed orbitals support donor-to-acceptor CT; orthogonal calculated geometry has a dark HOMO-LUMO transition, which gains small oscillator strength at crystal-like angles.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Ground-state/TD-DFT calculations, not direct measurement of excited-state geometry.

reference_evidence_units.quote: with a quantum yield close to 0.02% and a maximum at 366 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMIM solution
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Room-temperature dilute cyclohexane; main text discusses SI solution spectrum.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Solution emission is very weak; crystal emission is instead broad, peaking at 605 nm for O-DMIM and 549 nm for G-DMIM.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: SI not inspected; do not substitute abstract chloroform context for the detailed cyclohexane experiment.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The measured quantum yields are 1% and 3.5% for G-DMIM and O-DMIM, respectively.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMIM crystals
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Front-face illumination at 370 nm, calibrated against DCM dye in ethanol.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Estimated crystal QY is 1% green and 3.5% orange.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Method assumes all excitation light is absorbed; not integrating-sphere absolute QY.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Re-puried and recrystallized samples afforded the same results.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMIM purity control
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Re-purification and recrystallization, solid emission.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors report reproduced spectra, arguing against impurity emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Does not independently determine CT versus intermolecular excited-state origin.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the charge recombination is expected to be in the inverted Marcus regime and can follow radiative decay route in addition to the non-radiative one.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMIM crystal CT emission
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Emission-band fitting and solution electrochemistry; rigid crystal assumption.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Source assigns crystal emission to charge recombination from CT states in the Marcus inverted regime.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Shared reorganization/vibrational energy constraints are modeling assumptions; no conical-intersection evidence.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the internal reorganization energy associated with the CS state relaxation to the ground state is more than six times larger for G-DMIM than for O-DMIM
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMIM crystal spectral model
reference_evidence_units.conditions: CT band-shape fits, Fig. 8; common outer reorganization energy 0.400 eV.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Fits give internal reorganization energies 0.33 and 0.05 eV for green and orange; source connects them to different packing relaxation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Conditional fit, not direct structural dynamics. Printed component-contribution percentages on this page are internally inconsistent and not used.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The origin of the effect for DMIM appears to be alter- ations in rate constants for non-radiative decay.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMIM polymorph rate comparison
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Emission-fit model versus lifetime/QY estimates.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors estimate about 2.6-fold higher nonradiative rate for green from fits, versus about 3.5-fold from lifetime comparison assuming similar radiative rates.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Main text reports SI calculation; multiexponential decay and assumptions limit use as definitive rate separation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: No photochemical changes were observed in UV− vis spectra collected before and after irradiation
reference_evidence_units.subject: organosilane measurement controls
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Approximately 1e-4 M dissolved solutions; stirred 2 mm cuvette; 360 nm pump, 200 fs time resolution.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Before/after UV-vis spectra show no detected photochemical change during transient measurements.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This controls persistent photochemistry, not ultrafast intermediate identity or aggregation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: they can all be classified as a charge-separated state
reference_evidence_units.subject: organosilane series
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Steady-state emission/excitation-derived reorganization energies across acceptors.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors classify emitting states throughout the studied series as charge separated.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Shared state character does not imply identical recombination kinetics; derived parameters depend on spectral assumptions.

reference_evidence_units.quote: 334, 360, and 368 nm for Si2s-2E, Si2s-E,C, and Si2s-2C, respectively
reference_evidence_units.subject: Si2s-2C with acceptor controls
reference_evidence_units.conditions: DCM steady-state absorption, Fig. 1.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Si2s-2C red-edge half-rise is about 368 nm; the authors place the optical sigma-pi* CT transition on this edge.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Half-rise is not an absorption maximum. Earlier E,C data are comparison, not target data.

reference_evidence_units.subject: Si2s-2C
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Table 1 global sequential fits, DCM, 360 nm excitation; table visually checked.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Fitted hot-state relaxation is 2.8 +/- 1.2 ps and charge recombination 237 +/- 19 ps.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Kinetic-model estimates from TA, not fluorescence lifetimes or directly resolved reaction coordinates.

reference_evidence_units.subject: Si2s-2C
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Table 3 global TA fit, cyclohexane, 360 nm excitation.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Relaxation is 2.4 +/- 0.5 ps and charge recombination 137 +/- 8 ps in cyclohexane.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Underlying cyclohexane TA traces are SI Fig. S7, not inspected.

reference_evidence_units.quote: we do not see an enhancement in the charge-recombination lifetime for Si2s-2C
reference_evidence_units.subject: Si2s-2C solvent comparison
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Cyclohexane versus DCM; weak charge screening in nonpolar solvent.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors attribute faster recombination in cyclohexane to increased electronic coupling; unlike Si4s-2C, target lifetime does not lengthen.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This explicit negative comparison prevents transferring the stronger-donor trend.

reference_evidence_units.subject: Si2s-2C
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Table 2, DCM; two Franck-Condon weighting schemes; visually inspected.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Estimated electronic coupling is 310 or 134 inverse cm depending on model.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Uses shared mean reorganization energy and simplified vibrational weighting; not an independent measurement.

reference_evidence_units.quote: stimulated emission band appears instantaneously for Si2s-2C but exhibits a lag or induction for Si2s-2E
reference_evidence_units.subject: Si2s-2C and Si2s-2E
reference_evidence_units.conditions: DCM femtosecond TA, Figs. 2-3.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Stimulated emission appears promptly for the dicyano target, unlike the weaker diester comparator.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Instantaneous means within instrument response, not zero-time molecular dynamics.

reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors propose 1:1 complexation, supported by Job plot and assigned [L+Zn-H]+ mass peak.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No resolved crystal structure; binding constant fit assumes this stoichiometry.

reference_evidence_units.quote: coordination of oxygen atom of phenolic hydroxyl, nitrogen atom of imine and nitrogen atom of thiazole ring

reference_evidence_units.quote: due to the interruption of the PET phenomenon on pure probe L

reference_evidence_units.conditions: Binding mechanism Fig. 3d; Zn(II) addition.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Chelation is proposed to interrupt PET and restore emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: pure probes L have only weak fluorescence intensity in the pH range of 2.0- 12.0.

reference_evidence_units.quote: After adding RPMI-1640 solution containing 100 μM Zn2+ and incubation for 15 min

reference_evidence_units.conditions: HeLa cells with L 10 micromolar, 37 C 24 h then Zn; Fig. 5.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Main results report no obvious fluorescence with L alone and blue fluorescence after Zn addition.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Methods p.4 says 100 mM zinc whereas results say 100 micromolar. Dose conflict prevents reliable biological-protocol reconstruction; endogenous Zn detection not demonstrated by this control.

reference_evidence_units.quote: ODNI started aggregating at 40% fw with redshifted intense AIE emission
reference_evidence_units.subject: ODNI
reference_evidence_units.conditions: DMF/water, excitation 350 nm; main-text discussion of SI Figs. S3-S4.
reference_evidence_units.statement: ODNI aggregation begins near 40% water with more than 5- to 8-fold enhanced emission; HNI remains molecularly dispersed up to 90%.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: SI not inspected; thresholds differ between congeners.

reference_evidence_units.quote: with two emission bands at 380 nm and 530-540 nm which could be assigned to π- π transition and excimer emission respectively
reference_evidence_units.subject: ODNI and HNI
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Very weak emission in nominally molecularly dissolved pure DMF, 350 nm excitation.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors tentatively assign the long-wavelength DMF band to excimer emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Preserve weak assignment but note tension with the stated molecularly dissolved condition; not proof that 465 nm nanosheet emission is excimer emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: AFM images displayed that the ODNI-NS had a height of ~8-10 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: ODNI nanosheets
reference_evidence_units.conditions: DMF solution added to water with vigorous stirring; dialysis removes residual DMF; FESEM/AFM Fig. 2.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Source reports sheet-like nanoaggregates with 8-10 nm height.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Thickness measurement does not by itself prove an exact bilayer; source molecular-length/bilayer geometry remains model-dependent.

reference_evidence_units.quote: All these interactions were almost abolished in ODNI-NS indicating the existence of NI cores in an amorphous phase in the NS.
reference_evidence_units.subject: ODNI nanosheet packing
reference_evidence_units.conditions: PXRD compared with naphthalic anhydride and octadecylamine; Fig. 3.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Loss of NA-like pi-stacking reflections is interpreted as amorphous NI cores; retained alkyl-chain reflections support chain-directed assembly.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No ODNI single crystal: HNI SCXRD must not be represented as ODNI crystallography.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The ODNI-NS suspension in water having strong and stable blue emission centered at 465 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: ODNI nanosheets with OVCs
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Water, p-xylene or mesitylene titration; Fig. 6, 20 micromolar ODNI, 350 nm excitation.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Aqueous nanosheet emission peaks at 465 nm and is quenched approximately 75% by 20 ppm p-xylene or mesitylene.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Not complete quenching; authors suggest some NI cores remain inaccessible.

reference_evidence_units.quote: favoring strong intermolecular π-π interactions between electron deficit NI core and electron rich phenyl derivatives.
reference_evidence_units.subject: ODNI nanosheet analyte interaction
reference_evidence_units.conditions: OVC association with nanosheet surfaces in water.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors propose hydrophobic and pi interactions bringing electron-rich analytes to exposed NI cores.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Surface-association model, not measured cavity inclusion or an exact stoichiometric host complex.

reference_evidence_units.quote: from 3.511 ns to 1.946 ns on addition of 100 ppm p-xylene
reference_evidence_units.subject: ODNI nanosheets
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Time-resolved emission in water; Fig. 6d visually inspected.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Lifetime shortens with p-xylene, consistent with an additional excited-state quenching route.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Lifetime alone does not uniquely prove electron transfer or exclude mixed static/dynamic quenching.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the process of a-PET from electron rich OVCs to ODNI-NS could be involved in the suppression of fluorescence emission.
reference_evidence_units.subject: ODNI OVC sensing
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Electron-deficient NI acceptor excited at 350 nm; OVC titration.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors propose acceptor-excited PET from OVC to NI for xylene/mesitylene quenching.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Distinct from donor-excited PET proposed for nitrobenzenes; not an intramolecular CT assignment.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The obtained HOMO value for ODNI was −6.565 eV
reference_evidence_units.subject: ODNI/OVC energetics
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Reported DFT frontier levels; Fig. 6f visually inspected and Table S3 referenced.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Calculated HOMO ordering is used to argue for a-PET from p-xylene and mesitylene.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Orbital energies alone are not measured transfer free energies or kinetics; SI computational details not inspected.

reference_evidence_units.quote: A steady enhancement in the hydrodynamic diameter of the NS with increasing analytes concentration
reference_evidence_units.subject: ODNI disaggregation control
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Main-text account of DLS versus analyte concentration, SI Figs. S22-S23.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Reported increasing size argues against disaggregation as the cause of quenching.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: SI DLS not inspected; the stronger claim that sensing is completely a surface phenomenon remains interpretation, not established solely by DLS.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the emission was switched “on” increasing the quantum yield of 1 at pH 6.8 to Φ=0.528.

reference_evidence_units.conditions: Water 1e-5 M, excitation 360 nm, Fig. 1; pH 10 to 6.8.
reference_evidence_units.statement: QY rises from 0.024 at pH 10 to 0.528 at 6.8; intensity enhancement 22.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Steady-state protonation-dependent response, not direct electron-transfer rate or ESIPT.

reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors propose amine-to-fluorophore PET quenching in base and suppression upon protonation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: PET switching mechanism takes place from pH 10 to pH 7.

reference_evidence_units.quote: according to the Kasha’s exciton theory with formation of J-aggregates.

reference_evidence_units.conditions: Discussion of target red-shifted aggregate band by analogy with previously reported 4-chloro naphthalimides.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors invoke prior J-aggregate/exciton explanation for the red-shifted target aggregate emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The obtained film was exposed successively for 2 seconds to HCl and NH3 vapours.

reference_evidence_units.conditions: Acetonitrile sprayed on glass, evaporated in air; Figs. 2-3 visually inspected.
reference_evidence_units.statement: HCl produces bright emission and subsequent NH3 returns it to low emission within the reported 2 s exposure protocol.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Vapor dose is not quantified; this does not establish cycling durability or aqueous pKa of the film.

reference_evidence_units.quote: with maxima at 472 nm for 1 and 480 nm for 2
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 1 with comparator 2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Solid films after HCl exposure; 360 nm excitation.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Target broad film emission peaks at 472 nm with enhancement 44; comparator 2 peaks at 480 nm with enhancement 48.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Authors describe combined monomer and aggregate emission; comparator values must not replace target values.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The better expressed AIE emission in 1 and 2 could be attributed to the hydrogen bonding ability

reference_evidence_units.conditions: Ethanolamine-bearing 1/2 compared with dimethylamine 3 in solids.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors tentatively attribute stronger aggregate emission to OH/NH hydrogen-bonding ability.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No target packing structure or motion measurement; retained as bounded packing-interaction interpretation, not automatic RIM.

reference_evidence_units.quote: in a pH window 2.5-1.5
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 1 on paper
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Acetonitrile-loaded filter paper dried and exposed to aqueous solutions; Fig. 4.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Paper-supported fluorescence switching requires strongly acidic conditions, unlike solution pH 10-7.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Authors leave detailed thermodynamic origin for future work; matrix context is observed but mechanism unresolved.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Compound 2 is well soluble in water

reference_evidence_units.conditions: Paper-strip aqueous testing.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Comparator 2 migrates rapidly into water; chlorinated target 1 paper is more stable, which source attributes to increased hydrophobicity.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Comparator solubility is not target aggregation or direct binding evidence.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The radiative rates obtained for both phases are very similar, the value for solution is slightly larger than the solid state rate.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPC
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Calculated spontaneous-emission rates in solution and crystal.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Radiative-rate enhancement does not explain the brighter crystal in this model.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The result concerns this computational comparison, not every possible sample condition.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the out-of-plane rotation of the phenyl rings with respect to cyclopentadienyl ring are hampered because of geometrical restrictions imposed by the packing
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPC
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Normal-mode and reorganization-energy analysis in solution and solid.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Packing restricts specific phenyl motions.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Model-based motion restriction should not be represented as a measured molecular trajectory.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The modes associated with the out-of-plane bending of the cyclopentadiene ring leading to the corresponding conical intersection are not significantly activated during the first 500 fs of dynamics.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPC
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Initial 500 fs of simulated excited-state dynamics.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The simulated early dynamics do not directly exhibit the CI-driving puckering motion.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This is a limit of the trajectory window, not proof that CI decay is absent.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In the molecular crystal, because the S1–S0 MECI is classically inaccessible, the relaxation through this mechanism is disfavoured.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPC
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Comparison of optimized CI energies in vacuum and crystal.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The calculated crystal energy landscape suppresses access to a puckered CI.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: CI geometries and correlation-corrected energies use different methods; the claim is qualitative.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the enhancement of emission in the solid state is associated with the minimisation of decay through nonradiative mechanisms.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPC
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Source conclusion from vibrational and excited-state calculations.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source attributes solid-state enhancement to suppressing nonradiative decay.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This is an interpretation supported by calculations, not a new experimental result.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the complementary descriptions provided the RIR and RACI models.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPC
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Conclusion discussing both descriptions.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The paper explicitly treats RIR and RACI as complementary accounts.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The two labels are not assumed to represent independent experimentally separated causes.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The crystal structure shows minimal π −π interactions and electronic ex- citations are not significantly perturbed by the crystal environment.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPC
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Source summary of the modeled crystal compared with isolated/solution descriptions.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source distinguishes crystal-induced motion restriction from a major change in electronic excitation caused by intermolecular interaction.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Crystal packing alone must not be converted into an aggregate-exciton label; this statement does not exclude all weak intermolecular coupling.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The sheet-like packing in the α-DCS crystal energetically encourages excited molecules to remain in their packing geometry
reference_evidence_units.subject: alpha-DCS

reference_evidence_units.conditions: Chloroform solution versus single crystal; source calculations use TD-omegaB97X-D/6-31G(d), PCM solution and OEEC crystal embedding.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Crystal packing is argued to block the solution-like CI distortion.

reference_evidence_units.statement: Quantum yield increases from 0.018 in cyclohexane to 0.27 in water aggregates, with lifetime increasing from 0.23 to 7.0 ns.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Approximately 15-fold yield versus 30-fold lifetime increase is crucial; these are not interchangeable enhancement metrics.

reference_evidence_units.conditions: BTHPB dilute solution and water aggregates, 10^-5 M, 360 nm steady-state excitation; cyclohexane/paraffin viscosity control, 355 nm flash photolysis, 360 nm femtosecond pump-probe in THF or polystyrene.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Nearly unchanged ESIPT emission energy and shape with solvent polarity argues against ICT for the cis-keto emitting state.

reference_evidence_units.statement: Target kF is 11.1 versus 10.6 x10^6 s^-1, while kIC falls from 41.7 to 1.3 x10^7 s^-1. Film kISC is 9.7 x10^6 and kRISC 1.0 x10^6 s^-1.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Derived rates, not direct independent rate measurements. SI equations not inspected; near-constant kF argues against radiative-rate enhancement as the principal cause.

reference_evidence_units.quote: a broad excited-state absorption (ESA) band in the range of 800–1000 nm can be observed in neat film
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMF-BP-PXZ
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Nanosecond transient absorption, deaerated THF versus vacuum-deposited film, 410 nm excitation; monitor 940 nm.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Film ESA lifetime is 1413.3 ns, near the 1.4 microsecond delayed PL lifetime. THF has no corresponding triplet-indicating signal.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Triplet assignment is the authors' interpretation of ESA; absence of detectable signal is not proof of exactly zero ISC.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the oscillator strength of S1 is almost zero (f = 0.0006)
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMF-BP-PXZ
reference_evidence_units.conditions: DFT/TDDFT; crystal-based QM/MM two-layer ONIOM with rigid surroundings, BMK/6-31G(d) initial calculation.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Computed S1 is nearly dark; other functionals also gave nearly zero S1 oscillator strength according to the main text.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Approximate model; SI functional comparisons not directly inspected.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the emission wavelength of DMF-BP-PXZ in solid calculated with the PBE0 functional is 525 nm with a relatively large f value of 0.0523
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMF-BP-PXZ
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Optimized S2 in solid-state model; comparison to crystal emission at 525 nm.
reference_evidence_units.statement: A brighter S2 transition matches the cited crystal peak, supporting the authors' anti-Kasha assignment.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Crystal peak is distinct from 548 nm neat-film peak. Calculation-based state assignment, not direct experimental state-resolved proof.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Since it is difficult for us to obtain the exact value of kIC of S2 → S1 by calculation
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMF-BP-PXZ
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Model nonradiative pathway in solution and solid.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors substitute S1-to-S0 kIC for the full S2-to-S1-to-S0 process; resulting values are 3.1 x10^10 s^-1 in solution and 8.8 x10^6 s^-1 in solid.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The uncalculated S2-to-S1 step is an explicit model limitation, especially for a claim of competing S2 fluorescence.

reference_evidence_units.quote: As for S2, it is a typical CT state
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMF-BP-PXZ S2 and T3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: NTO analysis in THF and solid.
reference_evidence_units.statement: S2 is assigned CT from dimethylfluorene to benzoyl; T3 has significant locally excited character.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Not a demonstrated TICT or separate PET reaction.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the energy gap between S2 and T3 is so small (0.22 eV) in solid
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMF-BP-PXZ
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Calculated singlet/triplet pathway in solid.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors identify S2-to-T3 as dominant ISC and T3-to-S2 as RISC; calculated kRISC is 7.2 x10^4 s^-1.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This differs from experiment-derived 1.0 x10^6 s^-1 in Table 2; do not present the two rates as quantitatively identical.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the intramolecular motions are restricted greatly, and thus the nonradiative IC channels are blocked
reference_evidence_units.subject: Three AIDF emitters including DMF-BP-PXZ
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Solution-to-aggregate/neat-film comparison.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Restricted motions suppress competing IC, allowing ISC/RISC and delayed fluorescence to become prominent.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: A bounded source mechanistic account. This does not establish conical intersections or aggregate-exciton emission.

source_documents.title: Anti-Kasha's Rule Emissive Switching Induced by Intermolecular H-bonding

reference_evidence_units.quote: TA initially shows a blue emission with a maximum at 416 nm together with a modest band around 465 nm.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TA (azulene-1,3,6-tricarbaldehyde)
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Neutral DMF, 5 x10^-5 M; excitation 365 nm; Figure 2 visually inspected.
reference_evidence_units.statement: TA initially has 416 and approximately 465 nm emission with QY up to 10% in DMF; small water fractions favor a strong band near 495 nm.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: 10% is the initial DMF yield, not the water-added aggregate yield.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the absorption band of TA underwent a negligible change along with the alteration of the water fraction
reference_evidence_units.subject: TA
reference_evidence_units.conditions: DMF/water titration, Figure 2b-c.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Nearly unchanged absorption leads authors to rule out H/J aggregation, excimer and exciplex mechanisms for the color switching.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Source exclusion is spectroscopic, not universal proof that every aggregate excited-state interaction is absent.

reference_evidence_units.quote: These observations further indicate the formation of hydrogen bonds between the TA and H2O molecules.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TA-water interaction
reference_evidence_units.conditions: D2O titration in DMSO-d6; NMR aromatic upfield shift about 0.05 ppm; FTIR 11% versus 84% RH.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors infer water-to-TA hydrogen bonding from NMR shifts/broadening and lower-wavenumber carbonyl/OH vibrations.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: NMR Figure 3a main-text account; FTIR Figure S13 only reported in main, not personally inspected.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the intermolecular H-bond clusters are responsible for the photophysical switching whereas the further formation of bigger aggregates results in luminescence quenching
reference_evidence_units.subject: TA-water clusters
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Small-water clusters about 20 nm by TEM/24 nm by DLS; excessive-water aggregates about 400 nm.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors distinguish water hydrogen-bond cluster switching from quenching by larger aggregates.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Not generic aggregation-induced enhancement or evidence of a new intermolecular excited state.

reference_evidence_units.quote: no emissive shifts could, however, be observed (only with intensity quenching) for the MA and DA systems with water added
reference_evidence_units.subject: Monoformyl MA and diformyl DA
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Water addition to comparator solutions, main account of SI Figures S15-S16.
reference_evidence_units.statement: MA and DA quench but do not reproduce TA's emissive switching.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Comparator results delimit the triformyl response; SI not inspected.

reference_evidence_units.quote: an absorption band with a wavelength of more than 600 nm can be observed without any near-infrared emission.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TA
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Dual emission and excitation/lifetime comparisons before and after water addition.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors infer a dark S1 and assign the observed shorter-wavelength bands to higher states. Different excitation spectra and band lifetimes support distinct states; emission is oxygen-stable.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The dark-state/state-number assignment is interpretive; lifetimes and oxygen control are SI results reported in main only.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the S4 and S5 1nπ* states become lower-lying than the S3 π-π* state
reference_evidence_units.subject: TA and model hydrates
reference_evidence_units.conditions: TDDFT/B3LYP/6-31G(d), continuum solvent and explicit 2/4/6-water models; main methods p6.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Hydration stabilizes n-pi* states and suppresses the S3-to-S0 branch, favoring S2-to-S0 emission; authors invoke some CT character for the red shift.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Approximate electronic-state interpretation, not proton transfer; explicit-water stoichiometries are models, not measured binding numbers.

reference_evidence_units.quote: No remarkable shift and switching of emissions can be observed when TA was exposed to methanol
reference_evidence_units.subject: TA with alternative hydrogen-bonding solvents
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Methanol and ethylene glycol controls, main account of SI Figures S24-S27.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Methanol does not reproduce switching; ethylene glycol also affects spectra little. Authors propose water-cluster amplification rather than any hydrogen-bond donor being sufficient.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: SI spectra not directly inspected; failure to switch is not proof of absence of all binding.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Similar emissive switching behavior was observed for a TA doped PVA/PAAS film
reference_evidence_units.subject: TA in polymer film
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 11%/84% RH exposure and water-drop/drying cycles, Figure 5.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Humidity switches film emission reversibly; direct water addition eventually quenches it and drying restores the original state.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Matrix is a moisture-responsive support; no independent matrix restriction-of-motion mechanism is established.

reference_evidence_units.quote: is here more pronounced than its rigidity effect
reference_evidence_units.subject: TA
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Conclusion of solution and film photophysical analysis.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors prioritize electronic excited-state stabilization over hydrogen-bond rigidification.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Does not prove zero rigidity contribution, but does not establish RIM as the emission mechanism.

reference_mechanisms.label: HOST_GUEST_INTERACTION
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Water binds aldehyde acceptors in proposed hydrogen-bond clusters and controls emission. Broad host/guest family used for solvent-analyte binding, not a cavity-inclusion claim.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Preserve the source's limited CT character/stabilization interpretation, without converting the background ICT-sensor discussion into a stronger target claim.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Water changes dark/bright state ordering and emissive branch balance; this overlaps the anti-Kasha mechanism.

reference_mechanisms.label: SOKR_ANTI_KASHA
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Main photophysical account is switching between S3- and S2-dominated emission, not S1 fluorescence.

source_documents.title: Anti-Kasha’s Rule Fluorescence Emission in (2-Ferrocenyl)indene Generated by a Twisted Intramolecular Charge-Transfer (TICT) Process

reference_evidence_units.quote: Figure 1 shows the emission of 1, with a maximum at 3.1 eV (400 nm)
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1 / (2-ferrocenyl)indene
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Toluene; absorption, emission and excitation spectra, Figure 1.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Emission peaks at 3.1 eV/400 nm, above the lowest absorption maximum at 2.7 eV/460 nm. Excitation spectra associate fluorescence with the higher-energy state.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Anomalous spectral relation supports the source assignment but does not by itself identify the emitting geometry.

reference_evidence_units.quote: We used double crystallized compounds
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1, 1-4CH3 and 1-6CH3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Purification control; source methods pp1-2.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Compounds were crystallized twice to reduce impurity contributions; calculations also reproduce the low-energy absorption band.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Purity precaution, not complete impurity exclusion. Target in toluene has reported fluorescence yield 2.8 x10^-2.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This demonstrates that the presence of the methyl groups has a great inﬂuence on the anomalous ﬂuorescence observed for these compounds.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Methylated derivatives 1-4CH3 and 1-6CH3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Toluene comparison with unmethylated target.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Methylation red-shifts emission to 2.95 and about 2.7 eV and lowers yields to 1.1 x10^-2 and 0.9 x10^-2.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Comparator values not assigned to target; steric and electronic effects both change.

reference_evidence_units.quote: these transitions can be described as a charge transfer from the iron orbitals to the indene and the cyclopenta- dienyl (Cp) moieties
reference_evidence_units.conditions: TDDFT ZORA/SAOP/TZ2P electronic transitions in toluene, orbitals in Figure 2.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The 3.50/3.63 eV transitions are assigned metal-to-ligand charge transfer, increasing negative charge on indene/Cp.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: MLCT character is not evidence for triplet phosphorescence or a separate PET quenching event.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the blue line state, the twisted intramolecular charge-transfer (TICT) state, describes a local minimum of energy
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Dihedral-angle excited-state scan; Figure 4a on PDF p4 visually inspected.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Rotation of indene leads to a model TICT local minimum from which the authors propose photon emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Vertical-excitation scans are not full nonadiabatic dynamics or definitive excited-state pathway proof.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The perturbed states are typical of a conical intersection.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1 and methylated comparison series
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Perturbed excited-state curves during indene rotation, Figure 4.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors identify CI-like behavior between excited states in the rotational scan and connect it with formation of an emitting twisted state.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No demonstrated restricted CI access or CI-mediated nonradiative decay. Retain the reported interpretation without relabeling it RACI.

reference_evidence_units.quote: using a time constant of about 1.3 ns, showing that there is only one emitting state.
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Toluene TCSPC at 400 nm, excitation 375 nm; main-text account of SI decay.
reference_evidence_units.statement: A monoexponential fit gives about 1.3 ns; authors regard it as consistent with one emitting state.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Monoexponential decay alone does not prove unique microscopic geometry; SI trace not inspected.

reference_evidence_units.quote: with an increase of almost 40% with respect to that recorded in toluene.
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Solvent comparison; main text p4 continuing p5.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Fluorescence yield rises to 3.9 x10^-2 in methanol and 3.7 x10^-2 in acetonitrile versus 2.8 x10^-2 in toluene, consistent with CT stabilization.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Solvent dependence is supporting evidence, not an isolated test of TICT; methylated comparators respond differently.

reference_mechanisms.rationale: Explicit MLCT-to-TICT interpretation combines orbital/rotational calculations with lifetime and solvent observations.

source_documents.title: A Reappraisal of Kasha's Rule
A Computational Protocol to Predict Anti-Kasha Emissions: The Case of Azulene Derivatives
Excited state dynamics of azulene and its derivatives: The impact of energy gap and vibronic coupling on anti-Kasha emission in solution

reference_evidence_units.quote: No sign of the S1S0 transition emission has been recorded on excitation at 220, 237, 269, 296 and 315 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: Azulene
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 2-methylpentane; steady-state room-temperature spectroscopy, Figures 3-5.
reference_evidence_units.statement: No S1 emission is detected across these excitation wavelengths; S2 emission appears with the same envelope and excitation matches S0-to-S2 absorption.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Source notes S1 emission in literature under low-temperature laser excitation; absence is condition-specific.

reference_evidence_units.quote: there is such a Franck-Condon shift on photoexcitation that the geometry for emission is distinct to the geometry for absorption.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Azulene
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Absorption/emission corrected for Einstein frequency factors, Figure 6.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors infer different absorbing/emitting geometries from absent mirror-image symmetry while retaining azulene as a true anti-Kasha exception.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Interpretation of spectra; no motion-restriction or aggregation experiment.

reference_evidence_units.subject: Azulene 1a
reference_evidence_units.conditions: TVCF rates using ADC(2) energies/dipoles and DFT frequencies, 298 K; Table 2 visually inspected.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Calculated S1-to-S0 kr=1.6 x10^6, kIC=1.9 x10^11 s^-1; S2-to-S0 kr=2.7 x10^7 and S2-to-S1 kIC=6.3 x10^8 s^-1; S2 yield 4.3%, S1 yield 8.4 x10^-4%.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Parentheses are external experimental values reused by F052: S2 yield 3.5 +/-0.4%, not a new measurement. Rates use harmonic approximations and gas-phase optimized geometries.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The vibronic features of the experimental S2 absorption and emission spectra are only recovered after the inclusion of HT effects
reference_evidence_units.subject: Azulene 1a
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Franck-Condon versus Herzberg-Teller spectral calculations, Figure 3.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Including HT terms improves vibronic spectral shape; FC-only spectra fail to reproduce positions/intensities.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Spectra are normalized and shifted to experimental 0-0 energies; shape agreement is not independent absolute-energy validation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: when comparing 1a and 1d, or 1b and 1e, they have almost the same S2-S1 adiabatic energy gap, but still a significantly different rate.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Azulene 1a and substituted series
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Computed S2-to-S1 rates versus energy gaps and reorganization energies.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors attribute deviations from a simple gap-only trend to nonadiabatic couplings and total reorganization energies.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No assumption that all derivatives have identical rates, yields or accepting modes.

reference_evidence_units.quote: by 20 ps 90.5 % of the excited molecules occupy the S2 state, whereas 9.5 % occupy the S1 state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Azulene Az
reference_evidence_units.conditions: LVC/MCTDH two-singlet model, B3LYP/TZP COSMO cyclohexane; selected 18 of 48 normal modes.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The simulated S2 population stays near 98% initially and reaches 90.5% at 20 ps.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Population fraction is not PLQY; excludes longer-time emission and full-dimensional nuclear dynamics. Symmetry-restricted model gives about 97% instead.

reference_evidence_units.quote: turning off Q33 halves the amount of the loss of the S2 population
reference_evidence_units.subject: Azulene Az
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Virtual mode-ablation simulations; Q16/Q33/Q39 dominate selected-mode early dynamics.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Removing Q33 leaves about 94% S2 population; removing all three gives 98.7% at 20 ps (Table 2). Removing Q16 or Q39 alone has little effect.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Turning model modes off is not physical restriction in an aggregate. No RIM claim is inferred from this virtual intervention alone.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the rate constant of the internal conversion depends not only on the electronic energy gap, but also on vibronic couplings and molecular structure.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Azulene Az with artificially changed gaps
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Az Hamiltonian with gaps changed to 1.10, 0.87 and 0.56 eV; Figure 6.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Gap-adjusted Az curves differ from actual substituted-molecule curves, supporting coupling/structure dependence beyond energy gap.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Hypothetical gap perturbations are controls, not measurements of derivatives.

reference_evidence_units.subject: Azulene and 2-substituted comparators
reference_evidence_units.conditions: F053 quotes external experimental reference 44 for solution PLQY.
reference_evidence_units.statement: F053 uses 2% for Az in its comparison, rather than F052's compiled 3.5 +/-0.4% or calculated 4.3%.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: External values reported in main, not freshly measured here. Do not pool different source conditions or replace experimental yields with 20 ps populations.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the S1 state of azulene decays rapidly via an energetically achievable S1/S0 conical intersection
reference_evidence_units.subject: Azulene S1
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Introduction's literature-based explanation, citing reference 45.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source explicitly invokes S1/S0 CI-mediated decay to explain absent S1 fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: A cited mechanistic account, not a CI optimized or trajectory demonstrated by this two-excited-state study. No claim of restricted CI access on aggregation.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Competing S2 radiation/IC and very rapid S1 decay rationalize state-selective emission; rates and early dynamics are model-dependent.

reference_mechanisms.label: RACI_CI_ACCESS
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Retain the explicit literature-based S1/S0 CI explanation with low evidential independence. This is CI-mediated decay, not proven RACI under aggregation.

reference_mechanisms.label: SOKR_ANTI_KASHA
reference_mechanisms.rationale: All three linked sources support a bounded S2 anti-Kasha account through spectra, kinetic calculations and early dynamics.

mechanism_decisions.rationale: No source-grounded restriction of intramolecular motion established for this target under the extracted conditions; emission or vibrations alone do not establish RIM.

mechanism_decisions.label: PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT

reference_evidence_units.quote: a new green emission with the largest emission wavelength of 530 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: A after irradiation
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Ethanol, 10 mg/mL; 365 nm, 10 W irradiation.
reference_evidence_units.statement: A develops green emission within seconds, strongest at about 1 minute. Reported PLQY is 1.6% in air and 3.8% in nitrogen; solution emission lifetime is 1.12 ns.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The emission belongs to a photoactivated species. PLQY is reported as the before/after irradiation difference; the approximately 48 h visual persistence is not the excited-state lifetime.

reference_evidence_units.quote: A redshift was observed in the emission with the increased polarity of the solvents
reference_evidence_units.subject: Photoactivated A
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Comparison of ethanol, THF and DMF discussed with Fig. S2b.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source interprets the polarity-dependent redshift as donor-to-acceptor charge-transfer character.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: SI solvent spectra were not inspected. This explicit interpretation does not establish a twisted geometry and must not be transferred to B.

reference_evidence_units.quote: A, B, C and D exhibited very weak emission and no obvious photoinduced emission in the solid powder state
reference_evidence_units.subject: A-D powders and A in PVA
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Neat powder; main text also reports A-PVA control.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Neat powders do not show the strong photoinduced emission; the source also reports no obvious photoinduced emission for A-PVA. High A concentrations quench radical emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: These results delimit the PMMA enhancement; they are not AIE. A-PVA and concentration spectra are SI reports, not inspected SI.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The emission lifetime of A-3-PMMA film was 0.92 ns
reference_evidence_units.subject: A-3-PMMA
reference_evidence_units.conditions: A-3-PMMA, reported as 3 mg A per 100 mg PMMA; irradiated film.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The film changes from weak approximately 403 nm emission to approximately 475 nm emission; the 0.92 ns lifetime supports fast rather than phosphorescent emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Do not confuse this loading with A-24-PMMA PLQY or A-6-PMMA stability controls. Figure 3b visually inspected; caption says 3 min, spectrum caption 50 min.

reference_evidence_units.quote: an obvious EPR signal with g value of 2.006 was observed
reference_evidence_units.subject: Photoactivated A-PMMA
reference_evidence_units.conditions: EPR comparison of films before and after UV irradiation, Fig.3e.
reference_evidence_units.statement: An EPR signal appears after irradiation and is absent initially, supporting radical formation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Figure 3e visually inspected. EPR establishes radicals but does not alone identify the emissive charge state or prove anti-Kasha emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: shifted to 1685 cm−1 in A-PMMA film
reference_evidence_units.subject: A-PMMA
reference_evidence_units.conditions: FTIR: carbonyl band at 1680 cm^-1 in A powder versus 1685 cm^-1 in film.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors interpret the FTIR shift as supramolecular interactions and assign PMMA a protective role against oxygen and nonradiative loss.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Figure 3f visually inspected. This does not uniquely specify binding geometry or demonstrate restriction of a particular internal rotor.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The calculated fluorescence of A and B originates from the anti-Kasha
reference_evidence_units.subject: A and B radical cations
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Quantum-chemical spectra compared with photoactivated films.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Calculated emission is assigned to D4-to-D0 for A at 497 nm and D5-to-D0 for B at 512 nm, not to the neutral precursor singlet fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Table S1 is reported in main text but not inspected. These are state assignments from calculations, not direct state-resolved experimental proof.

reference_evidence_units.quote: making the reason for slow internal conversion due to the large energy gap between corresponding states.
reference_evidence_units.subject: A and B radical cations
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Interpretation of isolated D4(A)/D5(B) states above lower doublets.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors propose that a large gap to lower doublet states slows internal conversion enough to permit higher-doublet fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No experimentally determined internal-conversion rate or complete dynamics is provided in the main-text evidence.

reference_evidence_units.quote: single electron transfer (SET) from dopant to matrix
reference_evidence_units.subject: A and B in PMMA
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Photoexcited dopants in a proposed supramolecular complex with PMMA.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The proposed film activation route transfers an electron from excited A/B to PMMA, forming the emissive radical cation; two-step photoionization is the alternative proposed solution route.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: SET is inferred from broad, method-dependent energy-level ranges, not measured electron-transfer kinetics. Figure 4 caption reverses the direction verbally; the mechanistic prose identifies dopant as donor and PMMA as acceptor.

reference_evidence_units.quote: When the photoactived A-6-PMMA film was placed in the air for 120 h
reference_evidence_units.subject: Photoactivated A films
reference_evidence_units.conditions: A-6-PMMA stability in air; separately A-24-PMMA irradiated for 3 min at 365 nm, 10 W.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The A-6-PMMA emission is reported to change little over 120 h; optimum A-24-PMMA PLQY is 0.74% in air and 1.0% in nitrogen.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Stability is reported from uninspected Fig.S14a. Do not substitute A-24 PLQY for A-3 decay measurements or equate ground-state radical stability with excited-state lifetime.
